summary: The shell is an "open plane" in Taste terms, and a well-built one. It folds by width. Below 768px there is a 52px sticky app bar and a 56px five-item bottom tab bar. From 768 to 1180px there is a 72px labelled rail with 56px tiles and 20px icons. From 1180px there is a 240px sidebar with rows 34px tall on a 36px pitch, 16px icons at 1.75 stroke and 13px labels at weight 500. The sidebar and the 56px toolbar sit on the canvas, divided by 1px inset hairlines (shadow-np-edge-*), not real shadows. The product and its scope are both named: the organisation name plus a mono "NabaPresence" caption at the top of the sidebar, and the client switcher in the toolbar. Counts appear only on queues (Inbox waiting, unread notifications). Canvas gutters are 20px on phones (px-5) and clamp(16px, 2.4vw, 32px) from 768px, so about 18px at 768, 25px at 1024 and 32px at 1440. The page h1 is 26px on touch and clamp 22-28px on a desk. The main departures from Taste are these. The toolbar mixes control heights (34px and 36px) and shapes (8px corners and full pills). The search trigger is 34px on a touch tablet with no 44px fallback. CountBadge fills the count with the green accent, which breaks the product's own "nothing else is green" rule. The app bar title and the toolbar trail do not share the page's left edge. The not-found state uses an icon in a tinted square. Several Taste conflicts are deliberate and documented, so they are reported as tensions, not defects: the current item's accent tint plus a 3px bar, the labelled 72px rail, the 13px desk label size and the 12px card radius.

findings.issue: The desk search trigger is fixed at h-[34px] from 768px and has no pointer-coarse override. Its toolbar neighbours do have one: the ClientSwitcher (client-switcher.tsx:135) and ContextHealthChip (context-health-chip.tsx:93) both use pointer-coarse:h-11, and NotificationsLink stays 44px unless the desk variant applies. So on an iPad or touch laptop at 768px or wider, search is a 34px target in a row of 44px targets. It passes the WCAG 2.2 AA 24px minimum but fails the product's own rule ('controls 36px, 44px on coarse pointers', from the identity spec) and Taste section 12 (44px touch targets).
findings.rule: Phone and touch: 44px targets, one control height per context (app-screens section 12 and section 13)
findings.fix: Add pointer-coarse:h-11 (or swap h-[34px] for h-(--np-control-h) with pointer-coarse:h-11, matching the switcher and chip) so every control in the tablet toolbar is 44px.

findings.issue: One 56px toolbar holds four control geometries. ClientSwitcher is h-[34px] with rounded-md (8px) and a border. ContextHealthChip is h-[34px] with rounded-full and a border. CommandPaletteButton is h-[34px] with rounded-md and a border. NotificationsLink is desk:size-9 (36px), rounded-md and borderless. The heights are hard-coded 34px values that ignore the system's own desk control token, --np-control-h: 36px (globals.css, desk block). The radii mix 8px with a full pill.
findings.rule: One control height per context; Taste title/filter rows cluster at 32 or 36 (section 4.4, section 13)
findings.fix: Set the switcher, health chip and search trigger to h-(--np-control-h) (36 on desk) to match the 36px bell, keeping pointer-coarse:h-11. Either give the health chip rounded-md like its bordered neighbours, or keep the pill on purpose because it is a status read-out rather than a control, and write that down in docs/components/README.md.

findings.issue: Counts on the phone tab bar, the More tab, the tablet rail tiles and the bell are filled 20px pills: bg-primary (accent-500 oklch(0.45 0.105 150)) with white mono figures. The identity spec (2026-09-23-operators-desk-identity.md:40-42) limits green to the primary action, focus, the current nav item and the selected row, saying 'Nothing else is green except the ok status'. The desk sidebar (nav.tsx:113) and the More sheet (more-sheet.tsx:266) show the same count as plain muted figures, so one number has two treatments depending on width. The badge also spends the accent on chrome rather than on data.
findings.rule: Colour on data, not chrome; pale-tint pill with dark same-hue ink (sections 9 and 13); the product's own one-green-accent rule
findings.fix: Restyle CountBadge as bg-accent-tint text-accent-ink (same hue, pale tint, dark ink), or as a neutral bg-ink text-canvas badge. Either keeps a 20px pill readable over an icon without spending the solid accent. Leave the sidebar and sheet plain figures as they are.

findings.issue: The current item stacks four signals: bg-accent-tint, a 3px bg-primary bar (before:inset-y-[7px] before:w-[3px]), font-semibold and text-accent-ink on both the label and the icon. Taste's default on light chrome is a neutral grey pill with the label unchanged; a left accent bar appears once in 23 screens and a weight change on 2. The identity spec (lines 40-41 and 131) documents 'accent tint plus a 3px left bar' as a deliberate choice that reads in greyscale and forced colours. The weight change and the accent-ink label are not part of that documented pair. They also change the label's width as the selection moves, and the More sheet (more-sheet.tsx:45) uses tint + semibold + ink with no bar, so the treatment differs between surfaces.
findings.rule: Section 3.2 active item: neutral pill, label unchanged
findings.fix: Keep the documented tint and 3px bar (tension, product decision). Drop aria-[current=page]:font-semibold from ROW_CLASS in nav.tsx and more-sheet.tsx so labels do not reflow, and give the More sheet's current row the same 3px bar so one 'current' grammar holds on every surface.

findings.component: PageFrame vs Toolbar and notices (left edge)
findings.issue: The toolbar (topbar.tsx:72) and the notice strips (shell-notices.tsx NOTICE_STRIP_CLASS) start their content at --np-page-pad-x from the content column's left edge. PageFrame centres a max-w frame with mx-auto. Example: at a 1440px window the column beside the 240px sidebar is 1200px wide, so a default-width page (1080) sits 60px further in, putting the h1 at x≈92 against the switcher and breadcrumb at x=32. At 1920px the offset grows to 300px (and 120px for width=wide). The client switcher, the trail and the h1 never share one left edge on a large desk.
findings.rule: One left edge, one right edge (section 4.2), with the top bar part of the shell (section 3.3)
findings.fix: Either left-align the frame inside the column on desk (drop mx-auto from wide: up, keep max-w) so the h1 lines up with the toolbar's pad-x, or cap the toolbar's and the notice strips' inner content at the same max-w(--np-page-*-width) with mx-auto, read from the page's data-width, so the bars and the page share edges.

findings.issue: The phone app bar row is pl-2 (8px), and the workspace-name and title-echo cells add px-1, so their text starts at x=12px. The page below uses px-5 (20px, page-frame.tsx:47) and the notice strips also use px-5. The bar's title and the page's h1 and rows are 8px apart, a visible step on every phone screen.
findings.rule: One left edge (section 4.2); phone margins of 16-20px (section 12)
findings.fix: Keep the back control's -ml/pl tuning for its 44px hit, but give the title cells (data-slot workspace-name and app-bar-heading) padding that lands their text at 20px when there is no back link (for example pl-5 on the lead, or px-3 on the cells), so the bar's text sits on the page's 20px edge.

findings.issue: From 768px the gutters use separate fluid values: --np-page-pad-x clamp(16px, 2.4vw, 32px) gives 18.4px at 768, 24.6 at 1024 and 32 at 1440. --np-page-pad-y clamp(16px, 2vw, 28px) gives 28 at 1440, while --np-gap-section is 24 and --np-gap-card is 16. At 1440 the frame therefore uses 32 horizontally, 28 at the top and 24 between sections, and the fluid vw values produce fractional-pixel gutters. Phones hard-code px-5/pt-6 (20/24) outside the token, so crossing 768px drops the gutter from 20 to 18.4.
findings.rule: One gutter: use one gap value horizontally and vertically (section 4.1)
findings.fix: Make --np-page-pad-y equal to --np-page-pad-x (or set both to clamp(20px, 2vw, 32px) in whole-pixel steps by breakpoint, e.g. 20/24/32), and have the phone branch read the same token instead of literal px-5/pt-6 so 767 to 768 does not step backwards.

findings.issue: The not-found message leads with a FileQuestion icon inside a 44px rounded-lg (12px) bg-fill square, which is the 'icon in a tinted square' pattern. Its h1 is text-title font-medium (16px desk, 17px touch), against the 23-28px page title every other screen uses through PageHeader.
findings.rule: No icon-in-tinted-square (section 14); every screen has an h1 at 18-48px (section 4.3)
findings.fix: Remove the tinted square (show the icon bare in text-ink-muted, or drop it, since system-page.tsx already says 'words first'). Set the h1 to text-section or text-page-title font-semibold so a 404 has the same title rank as any page.

findings.issue: 'All clients' is drawn as a Building2 icon in a bg-fill square: size-5 rounded-(--np-radius-tag) in the toolbar trigger, and size-8 rounded-(--np-radius-control) in the scope rows (client-switcher.tsx:376,382). That is a grey icon in a tinted square standing in for an avatar.
findings.rule: No icon-in-tinted-square (section 14)
findings.fix: Show Building2 bare at size-4 in text-ink-muted in the avatar slot (it already aligns as the leading glyph), or reuse ClientAvatar's neutral variant so the two entries share one shape.

findings.issue: When Notifications lives in More, its unread count rides on the More tab as a bare number. The noun is in a hidden description ('3 unread notifications') but not on screen: a sighted user sees 'More 3'.
findings.rule: Counts on nav items only when the noun is clear from the label (section 3.2 house rule)
findings.fix: Show a dot instead of a figure on More (a 8px bg-accent-ink or bg-ink dot, the count staying in the description) and keep the number on the Notifications row inside the More sheet, where its label names it.

findings.issue: Under the desk variant, sidebar labels use --np-text-ui 13px at weight 500 (nav.tsx ROW_CLASS font-medium). Taste measured 14px at weight 400 on 12 of 16 sidebars. The 13px controls and 14px running text form a documented desk scale (2026-10-13 mobile-first spec and the globals.css desk block).
findings.rule: Section 3.2 rows: 14px labels at 400
findings.fix: Keep the scale (deliberate). Consider removing font-medium from the resting sidebar row (font-normal at rest) so the 13px label reads lighter like Taste's 400 and the active row's change stands out without the extra weight.

findings.issue: The tablet rail is 72px wide, with tiles min-h-14 (56px), 20px icons and a visible 12-13px caption. Taste's icon rail is 50-60px wide with 15-18px icons and tooltips. The product chose visible labels because iPads cannot hover (documented in nav.tsx:38-46 and the mobile-first spec line 122). The identity spec still says a '64px icon rail' (operators-desk-identity.md:95,130) while the code and the mobile-first spec say 72px.
findings.rule: Section 3.1 icon rail geometry
findings.fix: Keep the labelled 72px rail (deliberate and correct for touch). Update the identity spec's 64px rows to 72px so the documents agree.

findings.issue: --np-radius-card, --np-radius-panel and --np-radius-toast are 12px, and the menu radius is 14px. These are the 'weak middle' between tight (4-8) and soft (16-24). In this slice they appear in client-switcher-search.tsx:52 (rounded-(--np-radius-card)), the boundary alert (boundary.tsx:233) and the not-found icon square (rounded-lg = 12). The 12px card is a documented identity decision ('white cards drawn by a 1px line at radius 12').
findings.rule: Radius bimodal (section 13)
findings.fix: Record this as a tension, not a slice change. If the system moves, step --np-radius-card/panel to 16 (soft, nesting over 8px controls) and --np-radius-menu to 16, leaving tag 6 and control 8 tight.

findings.issue: The role in the account dropdown is uppercase mono with tracking-[0.02em] (e.g. 'OWNER'). The same role on Access denied (access-denied.tsx:255) is a sentence-case sans text-caption tag, so one datum has two styles, one of them an uppercase label.
findings.rule: Sentence-case labels; one pill style (sections 9 and 13)
findings.fix: Remove uppercase, font-mono and the tracking; use the access-denied tag classes (h-5 rounded-sm bg-fill px-1.5 text-caption font-medium text-ink-secondary) in both places, ideally as one shared RoleTag.

findings.issue: The 'Workspace' group label has pt-4 (16px) above it and pb-1 (4px) below, so Team and Settings sit 16px under the daily list rather than at the foot of the sidebar. Taste's sidebars give a group label 22-56px of air above and 13-33px to the first item, or push utilities to the bottom.
findings.rule: Section 3.2 groups
findings.fix: Raise the label to pt-6 (24px) with pb-1.5, or move the Workspace list to the bottom of the scroll area with mt-auto (the column is already flex-col with the account row below), so settings sit with the account row as in Taste's 'utilities at the bottom'.

findings.issue: Until sessionReady, the nav area renders null, and so do the toolbar's switcher, chip, bell and search and the main children. On a first anonymous visit the sidebar is the brand block over an empty 240px column, and the rows pop in afterwards. The organisation name already uses a flat bar placeholder (line 162), but the rows do not.
findings.rule: Loading = final layout with flat bars (section 11)
findings.fix: While !sessionReady, render a fixed set of flat placeholder rows (e.g. 5 h-[34px] rows, each a 16px bg-fill square plus a w-24 h-3 bg-fill bar, rounded-(--np-radius-tag), no shimmer) in the nav area, and hold the toolbar controls at their width with blank 36px slots, as AppBarScopePending already does on phones.

summary: The overlay layer is mature and mostly holds up against the Taste rules. One foundation (components/ui/overlay.tsx) drives Dialog, Sheet and AlertDialog. The scrim is flat with no blur and fades out faster than it fades in. Entrances animate only opacity, scale and translate, on house tokens. Every motion token drops to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion, and a global !important rule backs that up. Focus trap, return and Escape come from Base UI; QuickLook has its own finalFocus with a fallback. Footers put the primary last, sit right-aligned in a dialog and stack full-width in a sheet. The radius ladder is applied consistently: modal 16, sheet 20, menu 14, inset sheet 28. I found five real defects. (1) The shared Select/Combobox popup transitions `transform, opacity`, but Tailwind v4 writes `scale-[0.98]` to the separate `scale` property, so the scale snaps and only the fade animates. I confirmed this in the compiled CSS. (2) The docked ActionBar and the inline SelectionBar/ActionBar(surface) draw a 1px line and a shadow together. (3) ActionBar defaults to `tone="charcoal"`, so local, non-Google bars render charcoal (client-settings unfiled assign, listings-board 'Prepare bulk change'). That breaks the README's own once-per-screen, Google-only rule. (4) Docked bars use Tailwind's stock `ease-out` instead of a house curve. (5) The command palette's phone Cancel is 32px tall. The radius-12 'weak middle' (toast, bars), the hairline-plus-shadow menus and the green palette highlight are deliberate, documented choices, so I report them as tensions. Both specs also contradict the shipped tokens in two places (dark charcoal; which radius steps were retired).

findings.issue: The popup declares `transition-[transform,opacity]` but animates with `data-starting-style:scale-[0.98]` / `data-ending-style:scale-[0.98]`. Tailwind v4 compiles those to the standalone `scale: .98` property (checked in .next/dev/static/chunks/app_globals_css_*.css: `.transition-\[transform\,opacity\] { transition-property: transform, opacity }` and `[data-starting-style] { scale: .98 }`). So the scale jumps 0.98->1 on the first frame and only the opacity eases. The exit also keeps the 240ms `--np-duration-overlay` on ease-spring, while DropdownMenu and Popover leave on `--np-duration-fast` (140ms) with ease-standard. Select (35 importing files) and Combobox (4) therefore open and close differently from every other menu.
findings.rule: Motion is feedback: transform+opacity entrance, consistent overlay motion (app-screens §2 motion; README 'one ease-out, short durations')
findings.fix: Change the line to the DropdownMenu recipe: `transition-[opacity,scale] duration-(--np-duration-overlay) ease-spring … data-ending-style:duration-(--np-duration-fast) data-ending-style:ease-standard`. Better, have dropdown-menu.tsx:55 import menuPopupClassName and drop its private copy, so there is one menu popup recipe.

findings.component: ActionBar (docked on phone, and surface tone)
findings.issue: The base classes always add `shadow-np-pop`. The surface tone adds `border border-line` on top, so an inline surface bar has a 1px line and a 0 8px 28px shadow at once. When docked below md, DOCKED_CLASS adds `max-md:border-t max-md:border-line` but never removes the shadow, so a full-bleed bar fixed to the screen edge carries a hairline plus a pop shadow, in both tones. SelectionBar's docked drawing does add `max-md:shadow-none` (selection-bar.tsx:178), so the two bottom bars disagree.
findings.rule: A border or a shadow, never both; shadows only on what floats (§13 house rules)
findings.fix: Add `max-md:shadow-none` to DOCKED_CLASS (the hairline edge is enough at the screen edge). For `tone="surface"` inline, keep `shadow-np-pop` only while stuck and drop `border border-line`. Or, for an in-flow bar, keep the border and drop the shadow. Charcoal needs no border, since the tone step carries it.

findings.issue: From md the bar is `rounded-(--np-radius-card) border px-3 py-2 shadow-np-float`: a 1px `--np-line` border and `--np-shadow-float` (0 4px 16px /.10) together, and it is sticky at `md:bottom-3`. Nested radius: an outer 12px with 8px vertical padding wraps md tiles at `md:rounded-(--np-radius-control)` 8px. Concentric would be 12-8 = 4px, so the inner corners bulge.
findings.rule: A border or a shadow, never both; nested radii step down by the padding (§9, §13)
findings.fix: Keep `shadow-np-float` (it floats while sticky) and drop `border`, or keep the border and drop the shadow when not stuck. Give the md tiles `md:rounded-(--np-radius-tag)` (6px), or raise the bar padding to `py-2.5`, so 12 - 10 = 2 stays visually concentric. Either way the inner radius stays below the outer minus the padding.

findings.issue: `tone = "charcoal"` is the default. README line 35 says the charcoal bar is 'at most one region per screen, and only for the action that reaches Google'. Callers that omit the tone get charcoal for local actions: components/clients/client-settings.tsx:650 ('Add N to this client', a local assignment), components/listings/listings-board.tsx:1404 ('Prepare bulk change', a link to a local step; selection-bar.tsx documents that tile as never charcoal) and components/locations/booking-tab.tsx:975 (status 'Nothing is sent to Google yet'). Only 6 call sites opt into `tone="surface"`.
findings.rule: One near-black/accent surface for the one primary; accent/charcoal not on chrome (§13; README charcoal rule; identity D4)
findings.fix: Make `tone="surface"` the default and require an explicit `tone="charcoal"` on the Google-write bars (send-bar.tsx, editor-footer.tsx, review-detail.tsx, review-publish.tsx, bulk-operation-view.tsx). Switch the three local call sites above to surface. A dev-time warning when two charcoal ActionBars mount at once would enforce 'once per screen'.

findings.issue: `max-md:ease-out` is Tailwind's stock `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0, 0, .2, 1)` (compiled CSS line 131), not a house curve. globals.css only maps `ease-out-strong`, `ease-standard` and `ease-spring`. So the 320ms docked bar rise uses a different curve from the sheet it imitates (`ease-out-strong`, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)). The same class is at selection-bar.tsx:181. Exit is instant (`visible=false` returns null), so the bar rises over 320ms and then disappears in one frame.
findings.rule: One ease-out, house motion tokens (README 'Move with --np-ease-out'; §2 motion as feedback)
findings.fix: Replace `max-md:ease-out` with `max-md:ease-out-strong` in both DOCKED_CLASS constants. Either accept the instant exit as intended or document it in the component comment; don't add an exit animation that keeps a dead bar on screen.

findings.issue: The only button alternative to the swipe in the phone palette sheet is `<Button variant="link" className="absolute top-0 right-4 h-8! …">Cancel</Button>`. That is a forced 32px height on a coarse pointer, inside a 32px (`h-8`) row. Everywhere else the phone close/cancel is 44px (`--np-touch`): the overlay ✕ uses size=icon, the toolbar Cancel uses `min-h-(--np-touch)` and the takeover Cancel is 44.
findings.rule: Phone: 44px targets (§12); README '44px on coarse pointers'
findings.fix: Drop the `h-8!`, give the row `h-(--np-touch)` (or render the standard `OverlayCloseButton`/header ✕), and set Cancel to `min-h-(--np-touch) px-2.5`. If the row is to stay short, use an `after:` hit-area overhang like icon-sm does (`after:absolute after:-inset-y-1.5`).

findings.issue: Both disable with `opacity-50` and no reason channel. SelectionBarTile has no `disabledReason` prop; CommandItem uses `data-[disabled=true]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled=true]:opacity-50`. At 50% opacity, a 12px `text-caption` tile label on `bg-surface-alt` very likely drops below 4.5:1. README says 'Carry a visible reason whenever a control is disabled'; Button and DropdownMenuItem already support `disabledReason`.
findings.rule: Disabled controls stay readable and say why (task brief; README; WCAG 1.4.3 for informative disabled text is exempt but the house rule is not)
findings.fix: Add a `disabledReason` prop to SelectionBarTile that keeps the tile focusable, sets `aria-describedby` and shows the reason in `notes`, mirroring Button. Replace `opacity-50` with `data-disabled:text-ink-muted`, which is how menuRowClassName does it. Do the same for CommandItem, with a caption line under the label.

findings.issue: The menu/select/popover phone sheet puts its ✕ at `absolute top-5 right-2` (20px/8px). Every Dialog/Sheet uses `overlayCloseButtonClassName` = `top-3.5 right-3.5` (14px/14px). overlay.tsx says 'One recipe for every overlay', but the close moves 6px between a Select sheet and a Dialog sheet opened from it. The menu sheet also draws the OverlayGrabber although Base UI menus have no swipe (comment at line 160), so it shows a drag handle that does nothing.
findings.rule: One anatomy per context / honest affordances (§13 icons as single affordance)
findings.fix: Position MenuSheetClose with `right-3.5` and compute top as grabber height + (44-control)/2. Or reuse `overlayCloseButtonClassName` with a top offset of `top-[calc(--spacing(5)+--spacing(0))]` so only the vertical value differs. Either wire Base UI's drawer swipe into the menu sheet or make the grabber visibly inert (shorter, `bg-line`) so it reads as a lip, not a handle.

findings.issue: `<dd>` values are right-aligned (`justify-end text-right`) but have no `tabular-nums`. Counts, ratings and dates stacked in the divided facts list therefore use proportional figures and their digits misalign row to row. README says figures/counts/timestamps are tabular (`font-mono tabular-nums` or sans tabular-nums).
findings.rule: Right-aligned tabular numbers (§7, §13)
findings.fix: Add `tabular-nums` to the dd className. Callers that pass StatusPill etc. are unaffected.

findings.issue: Every floating menu and popover is `rounded-menu border border-line bg-surface … shadow-np-float`, a 1px line plus a 0 4px 16px shadow. The Taste table says 'a border or a shadow, never both'. The code comments cite Notion Mail's popover menu: 'hairline edge … the soft float shadow' (D3, opaque).
findings.rule: A border or a shadow, never both (§9/§13)
findings.fix: Tension: on a white surface over a white card the shadow alone at /.10 gives a weak edge, and in dark `--np-shadow-float` is nearly invisible, so the hairline is doing the work. Inside the token system, either keep the border and use `--np-shadow-pop` only in light, or swap the border for `shadow-[var(--np-shadow-hairline),var(--np-shadow-float)]`. That puts the line in the shadow stack, one elevation token, no layout border. Record the decision in docs/components/README.md either way.

findings.issue: Toast `--np-radius-toast: 12px` and the bars on `--np-radius-card: 12px` sit in the 11-12 'weak middle'. The menu at 14px is neither tight (4-8) nor soft (16-24). The identity spec (2026-09-23) fixes cards at radius 12 deliberately. The mobile-first spec moved the menu from 10 to 14 to sit under modal 16 / sheet 20 / inset 28.
findings.rule: Radius is bimodal: tight 4-8 or soft 16-24 (§9)
findings.fix: Tension, not a defect. If the Taste bimodality is adopted, the cheapest in-system move is to make the floating family soft: `--np-radius-menu: 16px` (rows stay 6 with a 6px inset, so 16-6 ≈ 10 ≥ 6) and `--np-radius-toast: 16px`. Keep in-flow cards at 12 or drop them to 8. Change it in layer 2 only; tests/design-system-contract.test.ts pins the values.

findings.issue: The highlighted palette row is `data-[selected=true]:bg-accent-tint data-[selected=true]:text-accent-ink` and its icon turns `text-accent-ink`. Every other list highlight (menuRowClassName, DropdownMenu, Select) uses neutral `bg-fill`, and README line 271 says 'Menu and select highlights use the hover fill, not the solid accent'. The keyboard cursor in the palette is chrome, not data, and it moves on every arrow press.
findings.rule: Colour on data, not chrome; accent on at most one control (§9, §13)
findings.fix: Tension with the docs' 'the current item and the selected row' accent allowance. Moving to `data-[selected=true]:bg-fill data-[selected=true]:text-ink` and keeping `[&_svg]:text-ink-muted` would match the menu recipe. Leave accent-tint only on a result that is the current page, if that state exists.

findings.component: Toolbar search Cancel and FilterButton badge
findings.issue: The touch search-mode Cancel is `text-accent-ink`, as is the command takeover Cancel at command.tsx:227. The active FilterButton turns its icon `text-accent-ink` and adds a `bg-accent-solid` count badge. That makes three accent marks on chrome in the toolbar row, on screens that already have a green primary.
findings.rule: The accent on data and at most one control; near-black primary (§13)
findings.fix: Tension: the iOS-style accent Cancel and the 'never colour alone' count badge are documented choices. Inside the tokens, drop Cancel to `text-ink` (it is a way out, not the primary). Draw the badge as `bg-ink text-surface` so the count still shows without the accent, and keep accent for the page's one primary.

findings.issue: README:37 and the identity spec:104 say 'In dark the charcoal role is near-white with dark text', but globals.css:819 sets dark `--np-charcoal: oklch(0.3 0.016 240)` with light ink ('The dark bar stays charcoal (D4)'), and tooltip.tsx:69 follows the CSS. findings.fix: Amend README.md (lines 37, 44-45) and the identity spec (lines 55, 104) to state: dark charcoal is a raised oklch(0.3) grey with light ink; the radius ladder is tag 6 / control 8 / card 12 / menu 14 / modal 16 / sheet 20 / inset 28; overlays move on 240/320ms. Rename or alias `--np-ease-spring` to make clear it does not bounce.

summary: I audited 30 display and surface primitives against Taste app-screen sections 7, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14, and against the documented NabaPresence system (globals.css layers, the operators-desk identity spec and the mobile-first spec). The base is strong. Cards use a 1px `border-line` and no shadow. Table headers are 12/13px medium, muted and sentence case, right-aligned over numeric columns, with tabular figures. Pill and badge colours come from one five-tone source (lib/ui/status-tone.ts) with gated contrast pairs. Empty and error states are separate, and LoadMore states the range. Defects: (1) `Skeleton` animates a travelling highlight, which Taste bans, and it is used in 44 files. (2) `QueryPending` puts a sentence above the skeleton, so the layout moves when data arrives. (3) `Empty` puts a 44px tinted square holding an icon at the top of 37 call sites; error states make that square red. (4) `KpiTile` shows "—" at page-title size, its hover adds a shadow on top of the border, and it colours every down delta red by default. (5) `PublishSteps` draws two status marks per row. (6) `ChartDataTable` styles its tbody row-header cells as header-band cells. (7) Table row rules and the selected-row fill do not match the list primitives. Three points are documented decisions and are reported as tensions, not defects: the 12px card radius (the weak middle; 12/14/16 stack up within 4px), the tinted table header band, and mono table figures beside sans KPI figures. I edited no files.

findings.issue: Every skeleton bar draws a travelling highlight. A `before:` pseudo-element uses `before:animate-shimmer before:bg-linear-to-r before:from-transparent before:via-surface/55 before:to-transparent` and the keyframe is `--animate-shimmer: shimmer 2s ... infinite` (app/globals.css:275). Only reduced motion stops it. Skeleton and SkeletonList are imported in 44 files, so this shows on nearly every loading state.
findings.rule: §11 Loading: flat grey bars at their real size, no shimmer gradient. §13 bans gradients on surfaces.
findings.fix: Remove the `before:*` classes so the bar is a flat `bg-fill` at `rounded-(--np-radius-tag)`. Keep the `shimmer` keyframe only for the indeterminate Progress bar (progress.tsx:83), or rename it to `np-indeterminate` so the skeleton cannot reuse it.

findings.issue: The glyph mark is a 44px square (`size-11 rounded-(--np-radius-card)`) filled with a tint (`MARK_TONE`: bg-fill, bg-success-tint, bg-danger-tint, bg-warning-tint), with a 20px icon inside. 37 call sites pass `icon={...}`, and `variant="error"` (15 call sites) or `offline` adds the mark automatically. Error states therefore lead with a 44px red-tinted square. Taste limits the negative colour to a small icon or the pill pair.
findings.rule: §13/§14: no icon in a tinted square or coloured circle. §11 Error: negative colour only on a small icon or the pill pair.
findings.fix: Draw the glyph bare: remove `size-11 rounded-* MARK_TONE[tone]` and render the svg at `size-5` in `text-ink-muted`. For bad/warn tones colour only the icon (`text-danger-ink` or `text-warning-ink`). Keep the `illustration` path as it is.

findings.issue: With a `label`, the pending state draws a `text-ui` sentence (20px line-height) and then a `gap-3` (12px) above the SkeletonList. The ready content has no such line, so the content jumps about 32px when data arrives. The default skeleton is always `SkeletonList rows={3}`, a bordered card at radius 12, whatever the real layout (a bleed list, a table, KPI tiles). Its bars are `h-3.5` and `h-3` (14 and 12px), standing in for a `text-body` title (16/24) and a caption line.
findings.rule: §11 Loading: the final layout with each value replaced by a bar at its real size; labels and headers shown at once; no layout shift when data lands.
findings.fix: Put the label in an `sr-only` `role=status` span, or overlay it, so it takes no layout space. Require callers to pass a skeleton shaped like their own content (DataTable header plus rows, KpiTile with a `h-(--text-page-title--line-height)` bar). Size the SkeletonList bars to the type tokens, e.g. `h-[1lh]` with a `text-body` wrapper and an inner bar at about 60% height.

findings.issue: The tile documents that a missing figure is "—", and reply-figures.tsx:251,276 passes "—" as `value`. It renders at `text-page-title` (26px on touch, up to 28px on desk) in `font-semibold text-ink`, so a full-size dash reads as a figure still loading.
findings.rule: §11: a missing value is a grey dash, never a dash at full value size ('--' at 24px reads as loading).
findings.fix: Add a `missing` prop, or detect `value === "—"`. In that case render the dash in `text-ink-muted font-normal` at the `text-section` size, inside the same `text-page-title` line box so the tile height stays the same. Keep the reason in `hint`. (The tile reasons themselves are an owner decision, R20 in the 2026-10-28 audit.)

findings.issue: On fine-pointer hover an interactive tile gets both `hover-fine:hover:border-line-strong` and `hover-fine:hover:shadow-np-raised`, a border and a shadow at once. `Card interactive` (card.tsx:39) states 'Flat: hover firms the hairline, never lifts the card', so the two primitives disagree.
findings.rule: §9.4/§13: a border or a shadow, never both; shadows only on what floats.
findings.fix: Remove `hover-fine:hover:shadow-np-raised` and keep the `border-line-strong` hover, matching cardClassName. Leave `transition-[...box-shadow]`, which the focus halo still uses.

findings.issue: `DIRECTION_DEFAULT_TONE` maps up to success and down to danger, so every falling figure is drawn in `text-danger-ink` with an arrow, even when the fall is good (a drop in response time) or trivial. The `tone` override is opt-in.
findings.rule: §7.5/§14: the sign lives in the text, not the colour; no red on every negative; status colour only on the fact that is failing.
findings.fix: Make the default tone `neutral` for every direction, keeping the arrow and the sr-only word. Callers that know the polarity pass `tone: "danger"` or `"success"`.

findings.issue: Each step row draws a 20px tinted circle with a glyph (`OUTCOME_VISUAL.mark`, e.g. `bg-danger-tint text-danger-ink`) and also a `StatusPill` in the same tone saying the same state. That is two status marks per row, and the tinted circle repeats down the list.
findings.rule: §7.6: one status mark per row. §13: no icons in tinted boxes repeated down a list.
findings.fix: Remove the leading mark span and its grid column (`grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto]`) and let the StatusPill carry the state. If a leading glyph is wanted for scanning, draw it bare at `size-4` in `text-ink-muted`, with no tint.

findings.issue: The visible table styles all `th` with `[&_th]:bg-surface-alt [&_th]:text-caption [&_th]:text-ink-muted [&_th]:font-semibold`. The tbody row headers (`<th scope="row">`, the identity column) match too, so the date or category column renders at 12/13px muted ink on the grey band, and only the weight is reset by `font-normal`. The header row is also semibold, while TableHead (table.tsx:368) uses medium. A missing value is passed as "—" (report-bar-chart.tsx:539) and drawn in full ink mono, not grey.
findings.rule: §7.5: the identity gets the primary ink and a missing value is a grey dash. §7.2: one header style.
findings.fix: Scope the band styles to `[&_thead_th]:` and give the row header `text-ui text-ink bg-transparent font-normal`. Use `font-medium` in the header to match TableHead. Render "—" in a `text-ink-muted` span (ChartDataTable can check for it).

findings.issue: Body rows use `border-b border-line` (neutral-200, oklch .9), the same strength as the header rule (`[&_th]:border-line`, table.tsx:306). ListRows and GroupedList divide with `line-subtle` (neutral-150, oklch .938), and DiffView flat uses `border-line-subtle`. Tables therefore have heavier row rules than every list, and no header rule stands out as the strongest line.
findings.rule: §7.2/§7.3/§9.2: row rules one step lighter than the card/header line (3-7% darker than the surface); the header rule is the strongest line.
findings.fix: Change TableRow to `border-b border-line-subtle` and keep `[&_th]:border-line` on the header. Make the same change for the `!flat` branch of DiffView (diff-view.tsx:107).

findings.issue: Selected table rows use `aria-selected:bg-accent-tint data-[selected=true]:bg-accent-tint`, a green tint. ListRow (list-row.tsx:520) and ListRowSwipe (list-row-swipe.tsx:246) mark selection with `bg-fill`, so the same state is green in a table and grey in a list, and the accent lands on chrome.
findings.rule: §7.8: the selected row takes the neutral --active fill. §9.2/§13: accent on data and at most one control, not on chrome.
findings.fix: Use `aria-selected:bg-fill data-[selected=true]:bg-fill` and keep `hover-fine:hover:bg-surface-alt` for hover, so selection is the same in lists and tables.

findings.issue: When `rows.length === 0 && empty`, DataTable returns only `{empty}`. The column headers and the surface card disappear, and the block changes shape when a filter clears it.
findings.rule: §11: an empty section keeps its frame and its header and adds one sentence spanning the block (grid-column 1 / -1).
findings.fix: Keep the `<Table>` and `<TableHeader>` and render the empty node in one `<TableRow><TableCell colSpan={columns.length + (selection ? 1 : 0)}>`, using `Empty size="sm"` with no mark.

findings.file: app/globals.css:563-575 (used by card.tsx:33, kpi-tile.tsx:143, alert.tsx:20, empty.tsx:145/179, table.tsx:266)
findings.issue: Cards, panels, alerts, toasts, KPI tiles, the empty mark, file cards and table surfaces all use `--np-radius-card: 12px`, which is the weak middle between Taste's tight (4-8) and soft (16-24) modes. Surface radii also stack within 4px: card 12, menu 14, modal 16, then sheet 20 and inset sheet 28. That is five panel radii where the inspector warns above three. The identity spec (2026-09-23 §37/§91) deliberately chose 'white cards drawn by a 1px line at radius 12', and the 2026-10-13 spec raised the menu radius from 10 to 14.
findings.rule: §9.4: radius is bimodal (11-12 seen on only 3 of 23 screens); nested radii step down; at most three panel radii.
findings.fix: Keep it inside the token layer. Option A (soft, which fits the touch-first sheets): set `--np-radius-card` and `--np-radius-panel` to 16px, `--np-radius-menu` to 16px (one value with modal) and toast to 16px, leaving control 8 and tag 6 so nesting steps 16, 8, 6. The ladder becomes 6/8/16/20/28. Option B (tight): card 8, control 6, tag 4. Either needs an identity-spec amendment.

findings.issue: The header cells sit on `bg-(--np-table-header-bg)`, which is `--np-surface-alt`, plus a bottom rule. This is a documented choice (the 'reference thead th sits on the sunken surface' note in table.tsx). Taste found no fill band on any of 11 headed tables. The type follows the rule: text-caption 13/12px, medium, muted, sentence case, h-10 (40px), numeric headers right-aligned.
findings.rule: §7.2 and §13: no header band; 12px grey sentence-case headers, with rules or space.
findings.fix: If the owner accepts it, set `--np-table-header-bg: transparent` in all three theme blocks (globals.css:712, 924, 1055). This is a single token change and keeps the `border-line` header rule as the strongest line. DiffView's `bg-surface-alt font-semibold` header would follow if it moves to the same token.

findings.issue: Table and chart figures use `font-mono tabular-nums` (JetBrains Mono), per the globals.css header ('IDs, codes and table figures are mono'). KPI values, GroupedList trailing values, LoadMore and RelativeTime use sans `tabular-nums`. The same review count can appear in sans on a KPI tile and in mono in the table below it.
findings.rule: §9.1/§13: a second face has one job, either every figure or IDs only.
findings.fix: Choose one. Either drop `font-mono` from numeric TableCell and ChartDataTable cells (sans tabular figures already align), keeping mono for IDs and codes, or apply mono to KPI values as well. The first option matches 'One voice' in the identity spec.

findings.issue: Each figure is its own bordered radius-12 card, and the docs describe them as 'rows of four', so a strip of four KPIs draws four boxes. This follows the documented reference `.stat` tile.
findings.rule: §9.4: group, don't box. A set of KPIs is one card split by 1px dividers.
findings.fix: Add a `KpiStrip` wrapper (one `cardClassName()` box with `divide-x divide-line`, and `grid-cols-2` with `divide-y` on phones) and a `bare` KpiTile variant without border or radius for use inside it. Keep standalone tiles for single linked figures.

findings.issue: A disabled swipe action uses `disabled:opacity-50` on a white label over `bg-accent-solid` or `bg-danger-solid`, which cuts label contrast to about half. Nothing says why the action is unavailable.
findings.rule: Brief: disabled controls stay readable and say why. §12 phone row actions.
findings.fix: Draw the disabled state as `disabled:bg-fill disabled:text-ink-muted` (a gated pair) instead of opacity. Add an optional `disabledReason` to `ListRowSwipeAction`, shown in place of the label or as `aria-describedby`.

findings.issue: The default variant is `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, the saturated accent fill with white text. No production call site uses it today (every one passes a variant), but a bare `<Badge>` would render as a saturated chip.
findings.rule: §7.6/§14: pale tint with dark same-hue ink; saturated fill only for the one rare call to action.
findings.fix: Change `defaultVariants.variant` to `secondary` (bg-fill with text-ink-secondary), and keep `default` available as an explicit opt-in.

findings.issue: The tag tones include `pink` and `purple` (and deprecated orange and green aliases). The only call sites are app/design-system/nm-list-demo.tsx:224-225; production uses `tone="accent"` once (booking-tab.tsx:482). The decorative `--np-tag-*` ramp and its contrast pairs (lib/design/contrast-pairs.ts:200-202) are kept up for a palette nothing uses, and purple is the violet the house rules ban.
findings.rule: §13: no violet or indigo; four hues at most per screen; colour on data only.
findings.fix: Remove `pink` and `purple` from TAG_TONES and map them (and orange and green) to `neutral` as aliases. Remove the matching `--np-tag-*` roles and contrast pairs once the demo is updated.

findings.issue: `size-7 rounded-(--np-radius-pill) bg-fill-secondary` is a 28px neutral disc behind each settings-row icon, repeated down the list (client-settings.tsx:142,173 and the design-system demo).
findings.rule: §13: icons in boxes repeated down a list, tinted or neutral, are banned; one plain 16px grey icon where it helps.
findings.fix: Drop the disc (`bg-fill-secondary rounded-*`) and render the svg bare at `size-4` or `size-5` in `text-ink-secondary`, keeping a `size-7` box so labels still align.

findings.issue: Every entry carries a 20px tinted circle (`size-5 rounded-full` with tone tint and ink), so a long history becomes a column of coloured discs, most of them for routine events.
findings.rule: §11: red is a signal, not a texture. §13: no tinted icon containers repeated down a list.
findings.fix: Use the 6px `bg-current` dot (already the default glyph at timeline.tsx:46) on a transparent ground, in the tone's `dot` class. Keep a glyph only for at-risk or attention entries.

findings.issue: Pills use `font-semibold` (600) at text-caption, and so do Badge (badge.tsx:28) and the KpiTile delta. With 52 importers, 600 is the most repeated heavy weight on list screens.
findings.rule: §7.6: pill text around 12px at 500. §9.1: a median of 3 weights per screen, with 600 used sparingly.
findings.fix: Use `font-medium` (500) for the `pill` variant and for Badge. The tint plus dot already carries the state, and the ink/tint pairs are gated for contrast at any weight.

findings.issue: The legend swatch uses a literal `rounded-[3px]` instead of a radius token.
findings.rule: docs/components/README.md:47: take shape from a radius token. §9.4 radius discipline.
findings.fix: Use `rounded-full` (a 10px dot, as in Taste's 'legend of dots') or `rounded-(--np-radius-tag)`, scaled down only if a token is added for it.

summary: This review covers the design system as a whole. The token architecture is sound. Layers 2–4 in app/globals.css never introduce a literal colour, and every component reads a role. 106/106 light contrast pairs pass in `pnpm check:contrast` (212 across both themes). The design ratchet holds token bypass at 103 findings in 42 files (R1 12, R2 9, R3 53, R4 12, R5 1, R6 2, R7 14). So a pilot can restyle most of the product by editing tokens instead of feature code. Card radius is a good example: `rounded-(--np-radius-card)` is written 102 times in 71 files, and all of them follow the token. Measured against the Taste app-screen rules, the main gaps are deliberate, documented choices, so they are reported as tensions: radius 12 cards, a 14 menu radius and a 28 inset sheet (the weak middle and above the soft band); a green filled primary, a green-tinted nav row with a 3px accent left bar, and accent count badges (accent on chrome); a sunken table header band; and a slightly blue (hue 240) dark theme. There are also plain defects. Skeleton uses a shimmer (46 importing files). `--np-ink-faint` has the same value as `--np-ink-muted` in both themes. Disabled states are opacity hacks (50/60/45%) that no token or contrast pair covers. Menus and popovers draw a border and a shadow together. Several tokens are never used (all four entrance animations, enter-stagger, the material/blur machinery, surface-raised/overlay, accent-active/vivid, line-focus, corner-shape). Finally, the docs disagree with the code. docs/components/README.md still requires serif titles, mono timestamps, ink pressed chips, a near-white dark charcoal and 36px controls, but the code has one sans (D1), sans tabular timestamps, accent pressed chips (chip.tsx:224-252), charcoal at oklch(0.3) in dark (D4) and 44px touch-first controls. The best pilot levers are in one place each: the radius block (globals.css:563-576), the `--primary`/`--sidebar-primary` aliases (765, 795), `--np-table-header-bg` (712/924/1055), the Skeleton primitive, a new disabled role, and the menu-surface recipe. Each one changes many screens without editing feature code. Dark-theme edits must go in both the `.dark` block (803-925) and its no-script twin (931-1057), and tests/design-system-contract.test.ts pins the token names and type values.

findings.issue: Every skeleton draws a moving highlight. It uses `before:animate-shimmer before:bg-linear-to-r before:from-transparent before:via-surface/55 before:to-transparent`, driven by `--animate-shimmer: shimmer 2s infinite` (translateX -100% to 100%). Skeleton or SkeletonList is imported by 46 files, so every loading state shimmers. The rounded-(--np-radius-tag) bars are also fixed at min-h-3/h-3.5 rather than sized to the real text.
findings.rule: §11 Loading: the final layout with flat grey bars at their real size, and no shimmer gradient
findings.fix: In Skeleton, remove the `before:` shimmer classes and keep `bg-fill` as a flat bar. Size the SkeletonList bars from the role line heights, e.g. `h-(--np-text-body-lh)` for the title bar and `h-(--np-text-caption-lh)` for the meta bar, so each bar matches the text it stands in for. Keep the keyframe only for indeterminate Progress (progress.tsx:83), where moving is the meaning, and rename it `--animate-np-indeterminate` so the skeleton cannot pick it up again. Add an R-rule or contract assertion that `animate-shimmer` appears nowhere except progress.tsx.

findings.issue: The ladder is 6 (tag), 8 (control/field), 12 (card, panel, toast), 14 (menu), 16 (modal), 20 (sheet), 28 (sheet-inset) and 999 (pill), plus literal rounded-[10px] on the segmented track and rounded-[7px] on its thumb. The most-used shape, the card at 12px (102 var uses in 71 files plus 15 rounded-lg), sits in the 11-12 weak middle. 14 and 10 are middle values too, and 28 is above the 16-24 soft band. Chips and segment items mix pill (999) with 12px cards, although the rule says pills go with soft cards only. The identity spec deliberately chose 'white cards drawn by a 1px line at radius 12' (operators-desk-identity.md:37), and the design-system contract test pins the token names.
findings.rule: §9.4 Radius is bimodal (tight 4-8 or soft 16-24; 11-12 is the weak middle); nested radii step down
findings.fix: Pick the tight mode, since it is closest to today's 8px controls, and change only layer-2 values: --np-radius-tag 4, --np-radius-control and --np-radius-field 6, --np-radius-card, --np-radius-panel, --np-radius-toast and --np-radius-menu 8, --np-radius-modal 12, --np-radius-sheet 16, --np-radius-sheet-inset 16. Add --np-radius-track: var(--np-radius-control) and --np-radius-thumb: calc(var(--np-radius-control) - var(--np-segment-inset)) to replace the 10px/7px literals. Change filter chips from rounded-(--np-radius-pill) to rounded-(--np-radius-control). Every card, field, dialog and menu then follows without feature edits. This is a tension: the identity spec's radius 12 has to be amended in writing (the amendment pattern used for D1).

findings.component: Accent policy (primary, nav current item, badges)
findings.issue: Green appears on chrome as well as on data. `--primary: var(--np-accent)` makes every default button a green fill (bg-primary in 20 files). The current nav item is `bg-accent-tint text-accent-ink` with a 3px `before:bg-primary` left bar, the exact pattern listed in §14. Count badges are `bg-primary`. --sidebar-primary and --sidebar-accent alias the accent too. Green also means 'healthy': accent-ink oklch(0.40 0.11 150) and success-ink oklch(0.43 0.11 150) differ by only 0.03 L, and in dark both are oklch(0.8 0.12 150). So a green 'Publish' button and a green 'Live on Google' pill share one hue but mean different things. The identity spec states 'One green accent: the primary action, focus, the current nav item (tint plus a 3px left bar) and the selected row'. Variant B, which reserved green for Google, was explicitly deferred in the mobile-first spec. On the product side, green on the one action that reaches Google is a recognised brand cue, and the contrast gate already passes it (7.08:1).
findings.rule: §9.2/§13/§14: the accent goes on data and at most one control; near-black primary; no tinted nav row with a left bar
findings.fix: Both sides should be on record, and the change is alias-only. Point `--primary` at `var(--np-ink)` and `--primary-foreground` at `var(--np-ink-inverse)` (dark: ink is 0.95, so the primary inverts to a white fill with a dark label, as Taste's dark default does). Keep the green for focus and data by leaving --np-accent and --ring alone. Optionally add a `brand` button variant for the single 'reaches Google' action. Point --sidebar-primary and --sidebar-accent at --np-ink and --np-fill. In nav.tsx:55-56 and more-sheet.tsx:45, swap accent-tint/accent-ink for `bg-fill text-ink font-semibold` and drop the 3px bar; better still, add `--np-nav-current-bg/ink` roles so the next change is token-only. Change count-badge to bg-fill text-ink. Record this as an amendment to the identity spec's 'One green accent' line.

findings.file: components/ui/button.tsx:35; chip.tsx:246; switch.tsx:24; radio-group.tsx:39; segmented-control.tsx:109; grouped-list.tsx:229; tabs.tsx:371; app/globals.css:1466-1468
findings.issue: No token covers disabled. Primitives use `disabled:opacity-50`, `data-disabled:opacity-50`, `opacity-60` (tabs) and `opacity: 0.45` (on-charcoal default button). At 50%, white text on accent (7.08:1) becomes light text on a pale green, roughly 2:1, and ink-muted (5.98:1) drops to about 2.3:1. The contrast manifest has no disabled pairs, so the gate cannot see any of this. WCAG exempts inactive controls, but the product's own rule (README: 'Carry a visible reason whenever a control is disabled') and Taste both expect a disabled label to be readable.
findings.rule: Disabled controls readable and say why; contrast gate completeness
findings.fix: In layer 2, add `--np-ink-disabled: var(--np-ink-muted)`, `--np-fill-disabled: var(--np-fill)` and `--np-line-disabled: var(--np-line)` (with dark equivalents), plus an `@utility disabled-quiet` that applies them instead of opacity. Swap `opacity-50` for that utility in the 7 primitives listed. Add pairs to lib/design/contrast-pairs.ts: ink-disabled on fill-disabled and on surface, at 4.5:1. Feature code needs no changes.

findings.issue: `--np-ink-faint` and `--np-ink-muted` are both neutral-500 (oklch 0.5 0.018 240) in light and oklch(0.72 0.014 240) in both dark blocks. The comment documents a four-step ladder ('faint is the last readable step'), but in practice there are three steps. The gate measures faint as a graphic (3:1) while it actually renders at 5.65-5.98:1, so the manifest describes a role that does not exist. It has 3 uses (breadcrumb.tsx:49, grouped-list.tsx:219, area-cards.tsx:325, plus a dot in reply-composer.tsx:782).
findings.rule: Text in three tiers, two greys that read apart (§9.2/§9.3); no dead tokens
findings.fix: Either retire faint (write `--np-ink-faint: var(--np-ink-muted)` as an explicit alias and mark it deprecated, update the 3-4 call sites to text-ink-muted, and drop its pairs) or give it a distinct graphic-only value such as `var(--np-ramp-neutral-400)` (L0.62, about 3.6:1, which suits separators and inert icons), keep the gate at 'graphic', and document it as never-for-words. Fix the ladder comment either way. tests/design-system-contract.test.ts:53 pins the role's existence.

findings.issue: `--np-table-header-bg: var(--np-surface-alt)` paints every `th` on neutral-100, a sunken header band, with a border-b line. The labels themselves already meet Taste: text-caption (12px desk / 13px touch), ink-muted, sentence case (D8), and numeric columns right-aligned with tabular-nums (table.tsx:369,437). The band comes from the reference ('--surface-2 … table head', identity spec token map line 71).
findings.rule: §13/§14: 12px grey sentence-case headers, no zebra, no header band
findings.fix: Set `--np-table-header-bg: var(--np-surface)` in :root and in both dark blocks, and keep the existing `[&_th]:border-b border-line` rule. That is one token and three lines, with no table.tsx edit. The `--np-ink-muted` on `--np-table-header-bg` pair then measures 5.98:1. Note it as a reference departure in the identity spec.

findings.issue: Menus, popovers and dropdowns draw `border border-line` and `shadow-np-float` together. The selection bar does the same with a card radius. An interactive KPI tile adds `hover:shadow-np-raised` to its 1px border on hover. Floating surfaces may carry shadows, but never a shadow and a border together.
findings.rule: §9.4/§13: a border or a shadow, never both
findings.fix: In the menu-surface recipe (inherited by dropdown and select) and in popover, change `border-line` to `border-transparent` and keep the 1px width. The shadow then separates the surface in light, the surface-overlay lightness step (0.24 on 0.18) does it in dark, and forced-colors still paints the transparent border as a system-colour edge. On kpi-tile, drop `hover-fine:hover:shadow-np-raised` and keep `hover:border-line-strong`. Fix the stale comment at globals.css:579-580: pop is not 'menus, dialogs, toasts', because menus and toasts use float and dialogs use modal.

findings.issue: The rule list every new primitive follows contradicts the code in five places. (1) Line 35-37: 'Serif (font-display, font-reading) only for page titles…' — globals.css:147-149 makes display/reading sans (D1 amendment, 2026-10-13). (2) Line 36-37: 'figures, counts, IDs and timestamps are font-mono' — D1 says list timestamps are sans tabular-nums and mono is only for IDs, codes and table figures. (3) Line 34: 'Pressed chips and the tab underline are ink, not accent' — chip.tsx:224-252 draws pressed and applied chips as accent-tint/accent-ink with an accent-ink ring, while kpi-tile.tsx:148 says pressed is 'an ink edge, like a pressed chip'. (4) Line 41: 'In dark the charcoal role is near-white' — globals.css:819 keeps charcoal at oklch(0.30) (D4); the identity spec repeats the error at lines 103-105. (5) Line 52-53: 'controls 36px, 44px on coarse pointers' — controls are now 44 by default and 36 only under desk. Line 39-40 also still forbids `caption-bar` and `--np-caption-bar*`, which no longer exist anywhere in globals.css or the code (grep is empty).
findings.rule: One source of truth; the existing system's own documentation contract
findings.fix: Rewrite the README rules from globals.css: one sans and no font-family in feature code; mono only for IDs, codes and table figures, with timestamps in sans tabular-nums; dark charcoal stays dark (D4); 44px touch-first controls and 36px under `desk`; drop the caption-bar bullet. Decide the chip question in one place: either change chip.tsx:252 to `bg-fill text-ink font-semibold ring-ink`, matching the README and kpi-tile, or amend the README. Add a contract test assertion that the README does not mention 'Serif'.

findings.issue: The spec's type table still lists serif display/page-title/reading at desk sizes only (body 14, ui 13). The token map says '--r-tag 6 / control 8 / card 12 / modal 16', which is right, but also says 'coarse pointers raise --np-control-h … to 44px' and 'h-[30px]' for small controls, where the system is now touch-first with --np-control-h-sm, and '--rail-w 64', where globals has 72px (line 640). The mobile-first spec amends some of this, but the identity spec has no pointer to the amendment at those lines, and its own type table (mobile-first spec lines 71-81) still says serif until the D1 amendment at the end of the file.
findings.rule: Documented decisions must match the code before a pilot relies on them
findings.fix: Add 'Superseded by 2026-10-13 mobile-first + D1' notes inline at those rows, or update the rows: sans everywhere, 72px rail, touch-first sizes with a desk step-down, and h-(--np-control-h-sm). Change the 'Page title … serif' and 'Reading … serif' cells in the mobile-first type table to 'sans (D1)'.

findings.issue: These have 0 uses outside globals.css and the contrast manifest: animations --animate-np-rise, np-rise-lg, np-slide-in and np-fade (with their four keyframes); the enter-stagger utility (whose comment says 'capped at four steps (240ms)', though 4 × 50ms is 200ms); --np-duration-enter; --np-surface-raised and --np-surface-overlay (both white, equal to surface in light); --np-fill-tertiary (equal to canvas); --np-line-focus; --np-accent-active (equal to hover); --np-accent-vivid (gated at 4.01:1 as 'switch on-state, progress' but never used: switch and progress use bg-primary); --np-success-line; --np-corner-shape; --np-material-blur and --np-material-saturate; the material-sidebar and material-toolbar utilities. The prefers-reduced-transparency and @supports blocks map opaque materials to identical opaque twins. --radius-3xl and --radius-4xl both point at the sheet. --radius-xl (panel) equals lg (card) and has 0 uses. --ease-spring and --ease-spring-snappy are plain cubic-beziers named 'spring' in a system whose rules say 'never a spring' (about 40 uses). The identity spec (line 199-201) still says lib/motion/reveal.ts and enter-stagger 'remain for groups that already use them'; reveal.ts is still wired up, but enter-stagger is not.
findings.rule: No dead tokens; one name per meaning
findings.fix: Delete the unused animations, the enter-stagger utility, the material blur/saturate variables and both no-op material media blocks, plus surface-raised/overlay, fill-tertiary, line-focus, accent-active, success-line and corner-shape, in one cleanup commit, together with their contrast pairs and the SEMANTIC_ROLES entries in tests/design-system-contract.test.ts. Either use --np-accent-vivid for switch and progress on-state or remove it. Rename ease-spring-snappy to ease-standard and ease-spring to ease-out with a codemod, or keep them as documented aliases. Point --radius-3xl and --radius-4xl at the next step or drop them.

findings.component: Type scale near-duplicates and display ceiling
findings.issue: Touch ui/body/title are 15/16/17 and desk title/reading/section are 16/17/18: three sizes within 2px, told apart mostly by weight. That gives 7 touch sizes and 8 desk sizes. The desk `--np-text-display: clamp(1.75rem, 2vw + 1rem, 2.25rem)` reaches 36px, above the 34px app-title warning (3 files use text-display). The mobile-first spec adopted the touch-first numbers deliberately: 16px body stops iOS zooming on focus, and 17/28 reading is protected.
findings.rule: §9.1 4-9 sizes, cleanest scales 12/14/16/24; app type is not display type (h1 18-32, inspector warns at 34)
findings.fix: Keep the touch values. That is a tension, and the 16px field rule is correct. On desk, cap display at clamp(1.75rem, …, 2rem) (32px), and let `--np-text-reading` step to 1rem/1.625rem under desk so desk reads 12/13/14/16/18/22-28/32 with no 17. Both are one-line edits in the desk block; the contract test pins the caption/count/body values, which stay.

findings.issue: Under `[data-density=compact]`, `--np-control-h` is 30px and `--np-field-h` is 32px, so a button next to a search field in a compact DataTable or inbox toolbar sits 2px shorter than the field. Comfortable desk keeps both at 36 and touch keeps both at 44.
findings.rule: One control height per context
findings.fix: Set the compact `--np-field-h` to 30px, matching --np-control-h. If 30px is too tight for the 14px desk body with an 11px pad and 1px border, set both to 32px instead. Either way it is a one-line token change.

findings.issue: Dark surfaces are oklch(0.18-0.32, chroma 0.012-0.016, hue 240), a blue-black or slate ground that is a deliberate choice ('Built for dark, not inverted: a blue-black canvas'). Taste bans a navy or slate dark theme and asks for true neutral darks. The light theme's hue-240/250 cool paper (C ≤ 0.008) is within Taste's ground range.
findings.rule: §9.3/§13: no navy or slate dark theme; true neutral darks
findings.fix: If the pilot adopts it, drop the chroma of the dark surface, fill and line values to ≤ 0.004 while keeping L. Edit both the `.dark` block and the no-script twin, because tests/design-system-contract.test.ts compares them declaration by declaration. Contrast is unchanged because L is unchanged. Record it as a tension against the identity spec's 'blue-black'.

findings.issue: There are six chart hues: green 150 twice, grey 240, blue 250, amber 70 and red 27. Chart-4 to chart-6 reuse the info, warning and danger status hues, so a multi-series chart reads as status colours. Taste allows four hues per screen at most and one hue per chart. chart-6 is used in 1 file.
findings.rule: §13/§14: no rainbow charts, four hues at most, one hue per chart
findings.fix: Keep chart-1 to chart-3 (accent, light accent, neutral) as the default set. Redefine chart-4 as a neutral at a different lightness, e.g. oklch(0.75 0.01 240), and retire chart-5 and chart-6 (alias them to chart-3) so a series never borrows a status hue. Check the one chart-6 caller.

findings.component: Control border strength vs Taste default
findings.issue: `--np-line-strong` (neutral-400, L0.62) draws field and secondary-button edges at 3.43-3.63:1 against canvas and surface. Taste's default control border (#d1d5db) is about 1.5:1 and reads lighter. The product's choice follows WCAG 1.4.11 (non-text contrast of 3:1 for a field boundary) and is gated.
findings.rule: §9.2 lines in three steps (control border one step darker than the card edge)
findings.fix: Keep it. The accessibility requirement wins over the study median. Record it as an accepted tension so a pilot does not lighten it to #d1d5db-equivalent.

findings.issue: R4's fix text says 'z-index waits for the shared scale', but the z-* scale exists (globals.css:683-692, 1339-1368). It also recommends `rounded-xl`, which is the panel radius, the same 12px as rounded-lg, with 0 uses. R7's 'why' cites a '768 / 1180 split', where the shell now has three bands (48rem, wide 73.75rem) plus the controls, capsules, short, tall and desk variants. Nothing in the ratchet checks the Taste-level rules a pilot will add: accent outside the allowed places, a border plus a shadow on one element, opacity-based disabled states, shimmer, uppercase tracking.
findings.rule: Enforcement should match the current system
findings.fix: Update the R4 fix to 'use z-sticky…z-skip-link; rounded-sm/md/lg/2xl/full'. Update the R7 'why' to name md/wide and the custom variants. When the pilot lands, add an R8 'chrome accent' rule, which flags bg-primary/bg-accent-tint outside an allowlist (button.tsx, chip.tsx, selection), and an R9 'quiet disabled' rule, which flags `disabled:opacity-*`. Both start from a ratchet baseline.

summary: The action and input primitives are well built: they read their sizes from tokens (44px on touch, 36px under `desk`), name every icon-only control at the type level, add invisible hit areas that reach the 44px floor, and give Button a `pending`/`disabledReason` API. Measured against the Taste rules and the repo's own README and specs, six problems stand out. (1) Keyboard focus disappears on an invalid field. In the compiled CSS, the `aria-invalid:` border and shadow come after `focus:`/`focus-visible:` at the same specificity, so an invalid Select trigger shows no change at all when it takes focus (a WCAG 2.4.7 failure). TagInput does the reverse: on focus its error is replaced by the accent. (2) Disabled controls are drawn with `opacity-50`. That puts a disabled primary at about 1.8:1 and a disabled secondary at about 1.9:1, which breaks the Taste rule that disabled controls stay legible. (3) A pressed FilterChip is drawn in accent tint plus an accent ring, while the README and the identity spec say three times that pressed chips are ink. (4) The rule that a disabled control shows its reason as text is not met by the primitives. `DisabledReason` is exported but has no caller outside button.tsx. Tabs hide the reason in `title` and an `sr-only` span. Switch, Checkbox, Select, Segmented, ChoiceCard and OptionRow have no reason prop. (5) Fields use a second focus style (a 1px border change plus a 3px accent tint at about 1.1:1) rather than the documented `focus-halo`. (6) Button has 11 variants, but `on-dark` and `destructive` have no Button callers, `tinted` has one product file, and `outline` (57 uses) only aliases `secondary`. Several conflicts with Taste are documented decisions and are reported as tensions: the green-accent primary, 3:1 `line-strong` control edges, radius-12 cards, and Switch/ChoiceCard using accent for the selected state. Off-token literals remain: checkbox 5px, segmented track 10px and thumb 7px, tabs `h-10` at the desk, stepper 22px, OTP 20px text. There are also two checkbox drawings and two removable-tag drawings.

findings.component: Field chrome / SelectTrigger / OtpField / SearchInput (focus while invalid)
findings.issue: `focus:border-primary focus:shadow-(--np-field-ring)` and `aria-invalid:border-danger-ink aria-invalid:shadow-(--np-field-ring-invalid)` have equal specificity (class plus pseudo, against class plus attribute). The compiled CSS (.next/dev/.../app_globals_css...single.css, lines 5884-5903 against 6200-6208) emits the aria-invalid rules later, so they win. An invalid field therefore looks exactly the same focused as unfocused. For SelectTrigger, which has no text caret, keyboard focus is fully invisible whenever the Field has an error. The opposite happens in TagInput (tag-input.tsx:129-131): the unvariant `border-danger-ink` loses to `focus-within:border-primary`, so the error edge disappears on focus.
findings.rule: WCAG 2.2 AA 2.4.7 Focus Visible; Taste: honest error states; mobile-first spec 'Focus: the focus-halo ring'
findings.fix: Give the focused-invalid combination its own rule that keeps the danger edge and adds a focus cue, for example in fieldChromeClassName and selectTriggerClassName: `aria-invalid:focus-visible:shadow-[0_0_0_2px_var(--np-surface),0_0_0_4px_var(--np-danger-line)]` (aria-invalid:focus:… on text inputs). Alternatively add a `--np-field-ring-invalid-focus` token in layer 2. In TagInput, move the invalid classes onto `aria-invalid`/`data-invalid` variants and add the same combined rule. Add a contract test that renders `<Field error><SelectTrigger/></Field>`, focuses it, and asserts that the computed box-shadow changes.

findings.file: components/ui/button.tsx:35 (disabled:opacity-50, data-disabled:opacity-50); also checkbox.tsx:78, radio-group.tsx, switch.tsx:15, segmented-control.tsx:109, chip.tsx:246, choice-card.tsx:47 (opacity-55), tabs.tsx:175/371 (opacity-50/60), label.tsx

findings.component: Disabled reason visibility (Button, Tabs, form primitives)

findings.issue: Fields signal focus only by changing the 1px border from `--np-line-strong` (L 0.62) to `--np-accent` (L 0.45), about 2:1 between states, plus a 3px `--np-accent-tint` ring (L 0.955 on white, about 1.1:1). Every other control uses `focus-halo`: a 2px surface gap and a 2px `--np-focus-ring` at about 4.3:1. That gives the system two focus styles, and the field's is the weaker one, even though fields are the most frequently focused controls.
findings.rule: Mobile-first spec 'Focus: the focus-halo ring'; WCAG 2.4.7 (passes, but weakly) / 2.4.13 intent; Taste: one system
findings.fix: Keep the border change but redefine `--np-field-ring` as `0 0 0 1px var(--np-focus-ring), 0 0 0 4px var(--np-accent-tint)`, or use `var(--np-focus-halo)` outright. That gives a 2px ring at 3:1 or better from the existing focus token. Mirror it for the invalid case with `--np-danger-line` (see the first finding).

findings.issue: `h-auto! border-0 px-0!` together with the base `leading-none` makes a default-size link button exactly one font-size tall: 15px on touch, 13px at the desk. Callers patch it one by one: active-filter-chips.tsx:171 `min-h-(--np-touch) desk:min-h-0`, review-detail.tsx:700 `pointer-coarse:min-h-(--np-touch)`, shell-notices.tsx:24 `min-h-8 pointer-coarse:min-h-11`. invitations-panel.tsx:743 passes only `self-start`, so it gets no patch.
findings.rule: WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 Target Size; Taste §12: 44px targets on a phone; README 'no target smaller than 24px'
findings.fix: Give the variant the same invisible overhang as `sm`, `relative after:absolute after:inset-x-0 after:inset-y-[calc((100%-var(--np-touch))/2)] after:content-[''] desk:after:inset-y-[calc((100%-var(--np-touch-min))/2)]`, and `leading-(--np-text-ui-lh)` instead of leading-none. Then delete the per-caller min-h patches.

findings.file: components/ui/button.tsx:67 (`lg: h-11`), 72; used in components/auth/*.tsx (21 of 21 lg uses, plus WRAPPING_BLOCK_BUTTON in components/auth/wrapping-button.ts:8)

findings.issue: There are 11 variants but only 7 distinct drawings. `outline` is byte-identical to `secondary` (57 uses in 27 files). `destructive` is identical to `danger-outline` and has 0 Button callers (all 59 grep hits are Alert or DropdownMenuItem). `on-dark` has 0 callers. `tinted` (an accent-tint button) has one product caller, components/settings/two-step-verification-card.tsx:154. findings.rule: Taste §8.3: one filled primary, a bordered secondary, a text tertiary; §13 'accent on chrome' banned; mobile-first spec principle 7 'One primitive per job'
findings.fix: Codemod `variant="outline"` to `secondary` and delete `outline`, `destructive` and `on-dark` from the cva. Change the one `tinted` caller to `secondary` and delete `tinted`. findings.issue: The tag is drawn as `h-7 rounded-(--np-radius-pill) border border-line bg-surface-alt`, which is both a border and a fill, and does not match RemovableChip (chip.tsx:453: `bg-fill-secondary`, no edge, `--np-chip-h`). The remove × is `size-6` with `after:-inset-1`, a 32px hit on touch, under the project's 44px touch floor (RemovableChip's × reaches 44 with `after:-inset-2`). findings.rule: Taste §13: pills are a pale tint, a border OR a fill; §12: 44px targets; README 'One primitive per job', hover-fine only
findings.fix: Render RemovableChip inside TagInput (it already has a labelled remove control and a 44px hit), or copy its recipe: `bg-fill-secondary` with no border, `h-(--np-chip-h)`, `rounded-(--np-radius-tag)` so it steps down from the 8px field, and `after:-inset-2 desk:after:-inset-1` on the ×.

findings.issue: Checkbox draws an 18px box with `rounded-[5px]` (a literal, not a token) and `border-[1.5px]`. OptionRow's checkbox indicator draws an 18px box with `rounded-(--np-radius-tag)` (6px) and `border-2`. A filter sheet (OptionRow) and a form (Checkbox) therefore show different checkboxes. Radio is shared through `radioClassName`, but the checkbox is not.
findings.rule: Taste: one radius family (nested radii step down); README 'Take its shape from a radius token'; mobile-first spec principle 7
findings.fix: Export a `checkboxBoxClassName` from checkbox.tsx (radius `--np-radius-tag` or a new `--np-radius-selection: 5px` token in layer 2, edge 1.5px) and use it in OptionRow's indicator, the same way radioClassName is shared.

findings.issue: The track uses `rounded-[10px]` and the thumb `rounded-[7px]`: literals that sit in the 9-12px 'weak middle' and differ from the 8px `--np-radius-control` of the buttons and fields beside them. On touch each segment is `h-(--np-touch)`, so the track is 50px tall next to 44px buttons and fields in the same toolbar row. The selected segment switches to `font-semibold`, which widens the label on select.
findings.rule: Taste §9.4: radius bimodal; §8.1: one control height per context; README 'Take its shape from a radius token'
findings.fix: Make the track `rounded-(--np-radius-control)` and the thumb `rounded-[calc(var(--np-radius-control)-var(--np-segment-inset))]` (5px, still concentric). On touch use an item height of `calc(var(--np-touch)-2*var(--np-segment-inset))` so the track is 44px, keeping the `after:` overhang so each segment is still a 44px hit. Reserve the bold width with a `data-text` ::after (bold, invisible, height 0) so selection does not shift neighbours.

findings.issue: Tab items are a hard-coded `h-11` on touch and `desk:h-10` (40px) rather than a token, while every other desk control reads `--np-control-h` (36px). A disabled tab is `opacity-60` and a disabled `<button>` tab is `opacity-50`, giving two disabled treatments in one file.
findings.rule: Taste §8.1: one control height per context; README sizes from tokens
findings.fix: Use `h-(--np-touch) desk:h-[calc(var(--np-control-h)+4px)]`, or add `--np-tab-h` (44/40) to layer 3 so the 40px is a named decision. Use the shared disabled recipe from the second finding instead of opacity.

findings.file: components/ui/button.tsx:40-58 (11 plain `hover:`), field.tsx:513, select.tsx:54, input.tsx:185, choice-card.tsx:44, tag-input.tsx:128/147, stepper.tsx:200/204/328, combobox.tsx:134

Tailwind v4's `hover:` only checks `(hover:hover)`, so a hybrid touch device can still leave a fill stuck after a tap, and primitives within the slice behave differently.
findings.rule: README: 'hover fills only for fine pointers (hover-fine:)'
findings.fix: Replace `hover:` with `hover-fine:hover:` in the listed class strings, including `hover:not-data-disabled:` becoming `hover-fine:hover:not-data-disabled:` in the button variants. Add a `check:design` grep ratchet for bare `hover:bg-` in components/ui.

findings.file: components/ui/button.tsx:35 and most primitives (`ease-spring-snappy`), checkbox.tsx indicator and switch.tsx thumb (`ease-spring`), option-row.tsx:71 (`ease-standard`); app/globals.css:604-607

The primitives use three easing utility names. `ease-spring-snappy` resolves to cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) (equal to `--np-ease-standard`) and `ease-spring` to cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (equal to `--np-ease-out`). findings.rule: README motion rule; Taste: no springs

findings.issue: Button has its own ButtonSpinner (size-3.5, border-2, `animate-spin` at Tailwind's default 1s) next to the Spinner primitive (700ms linear), so two loading animations run at different speeds. While pending, the label is swapped for `pendingLabel` and a 14px spinner plus an 8px gap is inserted, which changes the button's width (for example 'Publish' becoming 'Publishing…') and moves its neighbours in the ActionBar.
findings.rule: Taste §11: loading never shifts layout; README 'One primitive per job'
findings.fix: Render `<Spinner size="sm" tone="current" decorative />` inside Button and delete ButtonSpinner. Keep the width stable by laying the idle and pending labels in one grid cell (`grid [&>*]:col-start-1 [&>*]:row-start-1`, with the inactive one `invisible`).

findings.issue: `read-only:bg-surface-alt read-only:text-ink-muted` is the same drawing as `disabled:bg-surface-alt disabled:text-ink-muted`. A read-only value the operator may need to copy (an ID, a link) is greyed to look unusable, and nothing tells it apart from a disabled field.

findings.fix: Extend the selector list to `[data-variant="outline"], [data-variant="ghost-dark"], [data-variant="danger"]`, or define the override once as `& [data-slot="button"]:focus-visible`.

findings.issue: The filled primary is the green accent, `--np-accent` (oklch 0.45 0.105 150), used 161 times across 94 files. Taste prefers a near-black primary, with the accent kept for data.
