summary:
The data and admin slice is built on a disciplined token system. Tables use 12px (desk) grey sentence-case headers with no header band and right-aligned tabular numerics (Table `numeric`). Deltas are coloured by good or bad (delta-badge polarity), not by direction. There are no zebra rows, no uppercase labels (EYEBROW_CLASS is now sentence case), no sparklines, no gradients and no border-plus-shadow on resting cards. The settings save contract in policy-form.tsx already matches Taste 8.2: autosaving toggles, one save bar, or one card Save. The biggest gaps, measured from the code:
(1) The shared Empty glyph is a 44px tinted square. It reaches about 130 call sites in this slice through ReportingPanel/QueryError, plus 6 hand-rolled copies in auth, setup and the route error page.
(2) Disabled controls rely on `disabledReason`, which only renders a hidden span and a `title`. None of the 15 slice files that use it wrap the control in `<DisabledReason>`, and billing's Cancel subscription renders at 50% opacity with its reason invisible on touch.
(3) KPIs are one bordered card per figure, set at text-page-title, the same token as the h1. The 5-up grid leaves an orphan on phones.
(4) Loading uses a travelling shimmer, and a zero-review period swaps its tiles and charts for one icon panel instead of printing zeros and drawing the empty chart.
Several conflicts are documented decisions and are reported as tensions: card radius 12, one bordered `.stat` tile per KPI, Notion-Mail-style settings rows with icon discs and stacked sections, and the shimmer. The two report charts (ReportBarChart) are close to the rules: one green hue per chart (chart-1/2 differ in lightness, chart-3 grey), faint 3-line grid, legend only when there is more than one series, and a hidden data table. They miss on stacked-segment seams, the 6px bar top radius, per-point dots on the line chart, and sparse x labels.

findings.component: Empty glyph mark (via ReportingPanel/QueryError) and hand-rolled copies
findings.issue: Every empty, collecting, paused, off and error state draws its icon in a 44px tinted square: `grid size-11 rounded-(--np-radius-card) bg-fill|bg-success-tint|bg-danger-tint|bg-warning-tint`. It reaches about 130 ReportingPanel/Empty/QueryError call sites in this slice. Six more copies are hand-rolled: auth/sign-in-form.tsx:289 and auth/forgot-password-form.tsx:186 (size-11 rounded-lg bg-accent-tint), setup/step-done.tsx:45 (size-14 rounded-2xl bg-success-tint, 20px radius), setup/step-connect.tsx:327 and setup/step-notifications.tsx:27 (size-11 rounded-lg bg-fill), and app/(dashboard)/error.tsx:105 (bg-danger-tint).
findings.rule: 9.4 / 13 / 14: no icon in a coloured circle or tinted square; an error tint goes only on a small icon or in the pill pair
findings.fix: In MARK_TONE, drop the fill and keep the ink: render the glyph bare at [&_svg]:size-5 in text-ink-muted (bad tone: text-danger-ink) with no bg-* or radius. Replace the six inline spans with the same bare 20px glyph, or delete them, since the h1/h2 carries the meaning. AuthCard already has an unused `mark` prop (auth-card.tsx:243) that could be removed in the same pass.

findings.component: Button disabledReason across settings, billing, bulk and locations
findings.issue: Cancel subscription uses `aria-disabled:opacity-50` on danger ink. Its reason sits in a `hidden` span plus `title` only, so a touch user sees a half-faded red link with no explanation. Across the slice, 15 files pass `disabledReason=` (billing-card 239/334/356/366, plan-picker 216, bulk-operation-view 398, bulk-compose 1763/1893, hours-tab 560, menu-tab 340, posts-tab 376, posts-action-bar 463-515, lifecycle-workspace 185, suggestion-list 453-516, profile-editor 1618). Zero of them wrap the control in `<DisabledReason>`, the primitive whose own doc says the words must also be on screen because a title never shows on touch. plan-picker.tsx:200 prints the reason only when `reason === tooSmall`. The base Button sets `disabled:opacity-50`, which halves text contrast.
findings.rule: 8.1: disabled controls stay legible and say why; WCAG 1.4.3 for the visible reason text
findings.fix: Wrap each `disabledReason` Button in `<DisabledReason reason={…}>` (components/ui/button.tsx:334), or put the reason in the ActionBar `status` slot. For billing, render `manageBlocked` as a visible text-caption text-ink-muted line under the destructive action instead of a hidden span. Replace `aria-disabled:opacity-50` with `aria-disabled:text-ink-muted` so the label stays at 4.5:1. Some sites may show the reason elsewhere, so check each one, but none use the primitive built for it.

findings.component: KpiTile in report strips and the client hub
findings.issue: Each KPI is its own card (`rounded-(--np-radius-card) border border-line bg-surface p-4`): 5 cards in presence-figures.tsx:93, 4 in reply-figures.tsx:237 and 4 in client-hub.tsx:240. Taste's default for a KPI row is one container split by 1px dividers. The identity spec maps KpiTile to the reference `.stat` bordered tile on purpose.
findings.rule: 5 / 9.4 'Group, don't box': one container split by hairlines
findings.fix: Add a `KpiStrip` wrapper to ui/kpi-tile: one `rounded-(--np-radius-card) border border-line bg-surface` box with `divide-x divide-line` (2-up phone: `divide-y` plus a grid gap of 0), and let KpiTile take `bare` to drop its own border and radius inside it. Keep the standalone tile for linked or pressable cases if the identity wants them.

findings.issue: The default value uses `text-page-title` (26px touch, clamp 22-28px desk), the same token as the PageHeader h1. All 4-5 figures in a row are the same size, so none leads. On the client hub, four 26px counts sit under a 26px h1.
findings.rule: 5: KPI values 16-40px, median 24, and the answer figure leads at 1.3x its siblings; 8.2: usage figures stay smaller than the h1
findings.fix: Use `text-section` (20/18px) for strip tiles, which is the current `compact` size, and reserve `text-page-title` for a single lead figure via a `lead` prop. Example: Average rating on the reply tab at about 1.3x the siblings.

findings.issue: Five Google tiles go into `grid grid-cols-2`, then `@[40rem]:grid-cols-3`, then `@[60rem]:grid-cols-5`. Below 60rem that gives 2+2+1 and 3+2, leaving one orphan tile beside an empty half-row on every phone and tablet. reports-skeleton.tsx:38 copies the same grid.
findings.rule: 12: in a 2-column KPI grid the count after any lead is even, otherwise the last cell takes the full width
findings.fix: Add `[&>:last-child:nth-child(odd)]:col-span-2` at 2-up and `@[40rem]/report:[&>:last-child:nth-child(odd)]:col-span-1`. Alternatively, skip the 3-col step and go 2 to 5 with the odd last cell spanning, or render the strip as a divided list (label left, value right) on phones.

findings.issue: Every placeholder runs `before:animate-shimmer` (a travelling `bg-linear-to-r … via-surface/55` gradient, 2s infinite; globals.css:274-276). ReportsSkeleton also draws the tile labels as `h-3.5 w-20` bars (reports-skeleton.tsx:9) instead of the real label text, which is known before the data arrives.
findings.rule: 11: loading is the final layout with flat grey bars at real size, labels shown at once, no shimmer gradient
findings.fix: Drop the `before:` shimmer layer and keep `bg-fill` flat (the shimmer is documented in globals.css, so decide it there). In TileSkeleton, render the real label (`Search views` and so on) at text-ui text-ink-muted with only the value bar at h-8.

findings.issue: When the period and the prior period both have 0 reviews, the four tiles and both charts are replaced by one framed ReportingPanel (clock glyph in a tinted square, 'No reviews in this period'). The real zeros (0 reviews, a 0% response rate where defined, a dash for rating) and the empty chart frame disappear. ChartUnavailable (line 124) also swaps a chart for an icon panel.
findings.rule: 11: a real zero is printed; an empty section keeps its frame and header; an empty chart is drawn (zero line, no picture)
findings.fix: Keep the tile strip with values `0` and a grey `—` for undefined ratios, using the existing hints for the reason. Render ReportBarChart with the zero series (it already draws the baseline, the 3 gridlines and an empty readout) and put the one-sentence explanation in the chart card's figcaption.

findings.issue: Stacked columns (`flex-col-reverse`, no gap) put chart-1 oklch(0.52 0.13 150) directly on chart-2 oklch(0.64 0.1 150), and on chart-3 in the actions chart. The lightness gap of 0.12 between same-hue segments gives about 1.6:1 adjacent contrast with no seam, so the Search/Maps split is hard to read (presence-figures.tsx:155,176).
findings.rule: 6.4: stacked segments split by a 1-2px seam; WCAG 1.4.11 for adjacent graphical parts
findings.fix: In stacked mode, add `gap-px` to the column (or `border-t border-surface` on each segment after the first) so a 1px surface-coloured seam separates them. Keep `last:rounded-t-sm` on the top segment only.

findings.issue: The x axis prints only the first, middle and last labels, and the middle one is hidden under `@max-[22rem]/chart`, so phones get only the two ends. The y axis has 3 ticks ([0, 0.5, 1], line 373). Bars use `rounded-t-sm` = --np-radius-tag 6px (lines 473-474). Line mode draws an 8px dot on every point (line 460).
findings.rule: 6.3: 4-8 x labels, labelling only the two ends hides when things happened; 4-7 y ticks. 6.4: bars square or at most a 4px top radius; lines without point markers
findings.fix: Generate 4-6 evenly stepped x labels from `bars` (every ceil(n/5)th) and drop to 3-4 on phone, not 2. Use [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1] or niceMax steps for 5 ticks. Change bar classes to `rounded-t-[3px]` or `rounded-t-xs`. In line mode, draw the dot only for the picked/latest column.

findings.issue: A disconnected client row can carry up to four danger marks: the Health StatusPill (danger tone), 'Synced …' in `text-danger-ink` (line 497-501), 'needs reconnecting' in `font-medium text-danger-ink` in the Google login cell (line 908), and a `StatusPill tone="at-risk"` 'N failed' (line 884).

findings.issue: --np-radius-card and --np-radius-panel are 12px, with --np-radius-menu 14 and toast 12, the weak middle between tight (4-8) and soft (16-24). Controls are 8px and modals 16px. The identity spec (operators-desk-identity.md:37) names 'radius 12' as its direction.

findings.issue: Each icon row draws a 28px `rounded-(--np-radius-pill) bg-fill-secondary` disc around an 18px icon, repeated down lists: settings-index.tsx:71 (every area row) and member-sheet.tsx:113-164 (7 rows). This is a documented Notion Mail adoption (D6).

findings.fix: Render the icon bare at size-4 text-ink-muted in a fixed 16px slot (keeps the text column aligned via `indent`), and drop `bg-fill-secondary` and the disc.

findings.issue: Settings render as a stacked heading (text-ui muted) above a full-width card at every width, never as a label column beside a panel on desk. Taste 8.2 describes a roughly 450px label/description column beside a roughly 700px panel. The stacking is a documented D6 choice.

findings.fix: Optional: under `desk` and @4xl, make `variant="group"` a `grid-cols-[minmax(0,18rem)_minmax(0,1fr)]` with the heading and description in column 1. Otherwise keep it and note the deviation.

findings.issue: Each product 'beat' puts its icon in a 36px `rounded-lg ring-1` box, repeated three times down the list. The statement uses `text-display` (32px touch, clamp up to 36px desk, line 131), above the 34px app-title warning. findings.rule: 13: no boxed icons repeated down a list; 9.1: app titles 18-32px; 8.1/8.3: one control height per context
findings.fix: Drop the ring box and use a bare size-4 icon in text-ink-muted-on-charcoal. Cap the statement at `text-page-title`. Use the default size (h-(--np-control-h): 44 touch, 36 desk) for auth submits so they match --np-field-h.

findings.issue: Linked or pressable tiles (client-hub WorkTile) add `hover-fine:hover:shadow-np-raised` on top of the 1px `border-line-strong` border, so they have a border and a shadow at once.
findings.rule: 9.4/13: a border or a shadow, never both; shadows only on floating things
findings.fix: Drop `hover-fine:hover:shadow-np-raised` and keep the border step to `border-line-strong` plus `bg-surface-alt` on hover as the affordance.

findings.issue: When the previous period is 0, a count delta renders '+4' in success ink with 'vs the previous period', which signals growth from nothing.
findings.rule: 5 Deltas: from a zero prior write '+4 (new)' in grey; status colour never on a zero or undefined change
findings.fix: In kpiDelta, when previous === 0 and current > 0, return `{ value: `+${n} (new)`, tone: 'neutral', direction: undefined }`.

findings.issue: The phone Stepper sits in `rounded-(--np-radius-card) border border-line-subtle bg-surface-alt p-1.5` inside the wizard Card, which also uses --np-radius-card. A 12px radius nested in a 12px radius does not step down.

findings.fix: Use `rounded-(--np-radius-control)` (8px) for the inner box.

summary: The slice is mature and largely honest about its states. Each screen answers its one question first: the inbox opens on Needs reply, the listings board puts health first, and a listing's overview leads with its health pill, then alerts, then areas. List and detail fold correctly on a phone (data-view, with Back returning to the saved scroll position), and errors stay inside their blocks. The biggest measurable departures from the Taste rules are in rows. The listings board stacks 3 to 6 tinted pills on a desk row (Health, up to 4 Waiting pills, Verification), and "Healthy" and "Verified" are green on nearly every row. Every notification row carries an amber "Open" pill, an unread dot and up to three 44px ghost buttons. In review rows, "Needs reply" is marked twice (the unread dot and a dashed pill), and on a phone a row grows to about 140px. Two inbox details have drifted from the product's own spec. The selected row is painted bg-fill, neutral-150, only one ramp step from the hover colour (surface-alt, neutral-100), not the accent tint the identity spec documents. The desk tick box only appears on hover, although the spec says it is always visible. Loading states are close to the house rule but not exact: the inbox route outline leaves out the quick-filter chip row, so the list jumps down when the page lands, and the notifications page and the listing editors fall back to three generic 52px SkeletonList rows. Some differences are deliberate, documented system choices and are reported as tensions: 12px card radius, the shimmer skeleton, the sunken table header band, hover fills on rows, the line-art empty states and hidden zero tab counts. Composites depend most on ListRow, StatusPill, Skeleton, Empty and QueryStates, which makes ListRow and Empty the most effective places to fix things.

findings.issue: A desk row draws up to 6 tinted StatusPills: Health, up to 4 PendingChips ('n changes to publish' pending, 'n Google changes' attention, 'n posts awaiting approval' pending, 'Failed publish' at-risk) and Verification. A quiet row still shows 2 green pills ('Healthy' or similar from listingHealthTone, and 'Verified' tone=healthy), so green is painted down the whole table, not used as a signal. The phone already collapses Waiting to one text figure (WaitingFigure).
findings.rule: 7.6 one status mark per row; 7.5 only identity and key number in ink, rest grey; 11 red/colour is a signal not a texture; 14 'a status chip on every row'
findings.fix: Keep one pill per row: the Health pill, tinted only when it is not healthy, with healthy shown as `StatusPill tone="neutral" plain` or grey text. Render Verification as `text-ink-muted` text ('Verified'), keeping `tone="attention"` only for 'Not verified'. On the desk, reuse WaitingFigure in place of PendingChips (text '3 waiting' in text-ink-secondary with tabular-nums, plus the single at-risk 'Failed publish' pill), and keep PendingChips for the quick-look panel, where the detail belongs.

findings.issue: The selected review row is painted `bg-fill` (--np-ramp-neutral-150), only one ramp step from the hover fill `hover-fine:hover:bg-surface-alt` (neutral-100). The non-colour cue is a 3px `before:bg-ink` bar. The active nav item uses `bg-accent-tint` (app-shell/nav.tsx:55). The identity spec says the selected row takes 'the accent tint and 3px bar' (operators-desk-identity.md:41 and :293), and contrast-pairs.ts:147-153 already gates every row ink against --np-selection-bg / accent-tint as 'text in a selected row', a fill this row never paints. The code comment says the accent is held back for publishing, which contradicts the spec.
findings.rule: 7.8 a selected row in a list that drives a detail pane takes the nav pill's --active fill, never confusable with hover or focus
findings.fix: In ListRow's selected branch, change `bg-fill hover-fine:hover:bg-fill` to `bg-(--np-selection-bg) hover-fine:hover:bg-(--np-selection-bg)` (already contrast-gated) and keep the 3px bar. If the team really means to keep the accent off rows, update identity spec lines 41/293 and the contrast manifest to match bg-fill, so the documentation and the gate check what the screen draws.

findings.issue: On a fine pointer the select box stays at opacity 0 until hover or focus-within, and the avatar swaps out on hover. Identity spec :293 says 'Checkbox always visible in its own 44px column', list-header.tsx:188 says 'On a desk the boxes are always showing', and the components README forbids hover-only actions. Bulk selection is undiscoverable until the pointer lands on a row, and the leading column changes under the pointer.
findings.rule: House: no hover-only actions; 7.8 checkboxes where bulk actions exist are visible (18px, 2px stroke); 12/WCAG 2.2 discoverability
findings.fix: When `canBatch && desk`, draw the box (drop the `desk:opacity-0 …` classes) and leave the avatar out of the row, as select mode already does (`selection.selectMode && showControl ? null`). Alternatively, keep a fixed 36px (--np-avatar-list) box column and drop the avatar on the desk. The header's select-all box already sits in that column.

findings.issue: Every row has a footer of up to 3 ghost Buttons ('Open review/listing', 'Mark read/unread', 'Resolve'), each --np-control-h (44px touch / 36px desk), under a 3-line ListRow (title+time, listing, line-clamp-2 description). An estimated phone row is 24+20+40+44+24 ≈ 150px, so about 4 rows fit on a screen and the list reads as a stack of buttons. The row itself is `interactive={false}`, so the main action is not the row.
findings.rule: 7.8 row actions: none, or one kebab, or an ink text action on line 2; 12 phone: row actions are text actions or one compact trailing button, five 44px blocks turned a list into a stack of buttons
findings.fix: Make the row interactive with `href={reviewHref ?? listing href}` so the main action is the row. Move Mark read/unread and Resolve into ListRow's existing `swipeActions` / `actionsLabel` '⋯' menu (the pattern review-list.tsx:388-405 uses). Keep the inline 'Resolve for everyone?' confirmation only while it is open.

findings.issue: Every open notification carries `StatusPill tone="attention"` (bg-warning-tint / text-warning-ink, dot shown) reading 'Open'. Under the 'Open' filter, every row repeats the tab in amber. The row also carries the unread dot (ListRow emphasis=unread), so there are two marks per row. The inbox already solved the same repeat with QUEUE_SAYS (review-list.tsx:41).
findings.rule: 7.6 one status mark per row, neutral states monochrome; 11 colour is a signal not a texture
findings.fix: Render 'Open' as `StatusPill tone="neutral" plain` (or ink-muted text), keep the tint only for at-risk kinds, and skip the pill when `filter === "open"`, as QUEUE_SAYS does. Show 'Resolved' as text-ink-muted with no pill.

findings.issue: The outline draws ViewHeader, then the search row, then 5 queue bars (`h-(--np-touch) w-24 rounded-(--np-radius-control) desk:h-(--np-control-h)`, i.e. 44/36px filled pills). The real band then adds a QuickFilters ChipRow (always rendered; --np-chip-h 28px touch / 24px desk, plus gap-3 12px), and the queue strip is unfilled text tabs h-11 / desk:h-10 (40px). When the page lands the list moves down about 40px on touch and about 40px on desk (24 + 12 + the 4px tab difference).
findings.rule: 11 loading: the final layout with flat bars at real size, no layout shift when data lands
findings.fix: Add a ChipRow of 5 `Skeleton h-(--np-chip-h) w-12 rounded-(--np-radius-pill)` after the queue strip, and draw the queue bars as `h-3 w-20` text bars inside an `h-11 desk:h-10` row (the textTabItemClassName box), not control-height pills.

On a phone the pill also drops to its own line (basis-full under 24rem) and the preview is line-clamp-2. A row then runs to about 5 lines: 12 + 24 + 2 + 20 + 4 + 24 + 2 + 48 + 12 ≈ 148px, against 56-92px for two-line rows with media.
findings.rule: 7.6 one status mark per row; 7.1 two-line rows 56-92px
findings.fix: When `needsReply`, never draw the pill, because the dot, the weight and the sr-only unreadLabel already say it; this extends the QUEUE_SAYS rule to every queue. On a phone, put the pill in the line-1 `meta` slot beside the time (nowrap, flex:none) rather than on its own line, so rows stay at 3 lines (about 100px).

findings.component: Empty glyph (used by inbox Statement, detail pane, notifications, inbox error)
findings.issue: The default glyph is a 44px (`size-11`) square at radius 12 (`rounded-(--np-radius-card)`) filled `bg-fill`, `bg-danger-tint`, `bg-success-tint` or `bg-warning-tint`, with a 20px icon: an icon in a tinted square. It shows on 'No review selected', 'No review open', 'No notifications yet' (BellOffIcon), the filtered/unknown inbox empties, and the inbox error (danger tint).
findings.rule: 13/14 banned: icon in a coloured circle or tinted square; 11 empty: one sentence in the frame
findings.fix: In Empty, draw the glyph bare: `[&_svg]:size-5` with the tone as ink only (text-ink-muted / text-danger-ink), and no fill or radius. Or pass `icon={null}` from these composites, so the pane says 'Pick a review from the list.' as text alone.

findings.issue: While pending, the page draws the default SkeletonList: 3 bordered rows, each min-h --np-row-h (52/44px) with two bars and no avatar slot, inside a bordered radius-12 card even on a phone, under a visible 'Loading notifications' line. The real list is full-bleed on a phone, with 36px leading discs, 3 text lines and an action footer per row, so everything moves when data lands.
findings.rule: 11 loading: the final layout with flat bars at real size, rows keep their pitch, no shift
findings.fix: Pass `pending={<QueryPending label="Loading notifications" skeleton={<NotificationRowsSkeleton/>}/>}`, where the skeleton is drawn by `ListRow interactive={false}` inside the same `ListRows bleed` wrapper, as ReviewRowsSkeleton does (review-list.tsx:690-736).

findings.component: AreaCards / ReviewPublish / NotificationRow leading icon discs
findings.issue: Each peer area card opens with a 28px (`size-7`) `rounded-full bg-fill` disc holding a 16px icon (one per area: profile, hours, menu, photos and the rest), in a grid of identical cards (GRID :46). Review & publish repeats it down its area list (`bg-fill-secondary`), and notifications repeat a kind glyph in a 36px bg-avatar-bg circle on every row.
findings.rule: 13 banned: icons in boxes repeated down a list or on top of every peer card, tinted or neutral; rows of identical cards with no icon on top
findings.fix: Drop the disc and keep a bare `size-4 text-ink-muted` icon before the title, or drop the icon, since the area name is the identity. In notifications, keep the leading column empty (ListRow without `leading`) so the text starts on the inset edge.

findings.issue: Beside a loading list, the detail pane shows a centred Spinner with 'Loading reviews'. A loading review draws two generic blocks (`h-28` and `h-44 w-full rounded-(--np-radius-card)`) that do not match the quote (text-reading lines) or the composer (6-row textarea, prompt bar), so the pane reflows when the review arrives.
findings.rule: 11 loading: final layout, flat bars at real size, no spinner-only blocks
findings.fix: Replace the two blocks with 3 `h-4` reading-line bars (the quote) and a composer frame: a `min-h-[calc(6*var(--np-text-reading-lh))]` bar plus a `h-(--np-control-h)` prompt-bar row. On lg, keep the inspector as the 'No review selected' statement in place of the spinner.

findings.issue: When the summary fails, the 'Google' group renders two SettingsRows ('Google connection', 'Last published'), each with the same sentence ('The listing summary didn't load…') and a 'Couldn't check' pill. The block has no Retry, even though ListingOverview has `onRetrySummary`.
findings.rule: 11 error: inside the block that failed, one sentence and a Retry text button
findings.fix: Render one caption row ('Couldn't load the Google summary.') with a ghost `Button` 'Try again' wired to `summary.refetch()`, passed in as a prop the way OverviewAlerts receives onRetrySummary, and drop the duplicated pills.

findings.issue: An in-app area switch shows 'Loading this page…' plus 3 generic 52px bordered skeleton rows, whatever the editor is (hours grid, photo grid, posts list, profile form).
findings.rule: 11 loading: final layout
findings.fix: Give each AREA_EDITORS `dynamic()` entry a `loading` that renders that area's own skeleton (the hours and profile editors already have row and field geometry), falling back to QueryPending only for areas without one.

findings.file: components/ui/tabs.tsx:193 (`desk:h-10`), components/ui/toolbar.tsx:251 (search `desk:h-(--np-control-h)` = 36px), components/ui/chip.tsx:242 (--np-chip-h 24px desk), components/ui/select.tsx:52 (field 36px); composed in components/inbox/inbox-toolbar.tsx:211-277
findings.issue: One control band stacks 36px search, 36px filter circle and owner select, 40px queue tabs and 24px quick-filter chips: three control heights in one context.
findings.rule: 8/13 one control height per context; 7.8 toolbar 30-36px
findings.fix: Set the text tabs to `desk:h-(--np-control-h)` (36px) in textTabItemClassName, or override it in QueueTabs, so the band has 36px controls and 24px chips.

findings.issue: The list total ('n listings · health summary') is `sr-only` unless the summaries failed. Sighted users get a total only from the 'All n' chip count.
findings.rule: 7.8 a full list screen states the total above the table
findings.fix: Always draw the count line as `text-caption text-ink-muted tabular-nums`, keeping the live region, and drop the sr-only branch.

findings.issue: The unread count appears in the ViewHeader title count and again as an 'n open and unread' status line beside 'Mark all read'. Together with the description paragraph and the filter hint, that is 4 lines of chrome above the first row.
findings.rule: 12 the first list row starts in the top 60%; 4.3 title carries the count once
findings.fix: Keep the ViewHeader count, which already carries countLabel for screen readers, and make the status line sr-only or remove it. Put 'Mark all read' on the tabs row.

findings.component: Button disabled state (Generate, select-all, load more)
findings.issue: Disabled buttons drop to 50% opacity. Generate is disabled whenever `!editable` (reply-composer.tsx:470) with no visible reason next to it; only the credits-exhausted case adds a caption.
findings.rule: Taste: disabled controls readable and say why; components README 'Carry a visible reason whenever a control is disabled'
findings.fix: Show the reason as a text-caption next to Generate when `!editable` (e.g. 'Publishing — editing is paused'), using the pattern of the `ai-unavailable` note at :583-590. At the primitive level, consider `data-disabled:text-ink-muted` in place of opacity-50, so labels stay above 4.5:1.

findings.component: Card radius 12 (notifications card, area cards, review-publish cards, quote block, board table surface)
findings.issue: Cards and panels sit at radius 12, which Taste calls the weak middle of its bimodal scale (tight 4-8 or soft 16-24). Nesting does step down (card 12, control 8, tag 6), so the nested-radius rule holds.
findings.rule: 9.4 radius bimodal; 11-12 is the weak middle
findings.fix: Documented decision: the identity spec says 'white cards drawn by a 1px line at radius 12' and retired the 14/16/20 steps (operators-desk-identity.md:37, :55). If the owner adopts the Taste rule, the single change is --np-radius-card / --np-radius-panel to 8px (tight, matching control 8 and tag 6, though nested radii would then be equal rather than stepping down) or to 16px (soft, stepping 16 → 8 → 6). No component edits are needed.

findings.issue: Every loading bar in the slice (review rows, queue counts, board cells, area cards) runs a travelling highlight. Taste's loading rule asks for flat bars with no shimmer gradient.
findings.rule: 11 loading: no shimmer gradient
findings.fix: Documented decision: the Skeleton docstring cites the reference `.skeleton` ('a soft highlight travelling across it. Reduced motion freezes it'). To follow Taste, drop the `before:` shimmer layer and keep the flat `bg-fill` bar. It is a one-line primitive change that propagates to the 44 importers.

findings.issue: The board's header row is a sunken fill band with a rule under it. Taste asks for no fill band: 12px grey sentence-case text on the surface. The text itself complies (text-caption, ink-muted, sentence case, h-10).
findings.rule: 7.2 header: no fill band; 13 'no header band'
findings.fix: Documented decision: globals.css says '`surface-alt` is the sunken step: table heads, card footers, rails'. To follow Taste, set `--np-table-header-bg: var(--np-surface)` and keep the border-b, which then becomes the table's strongest line, as 7.2 allows.

findings.issue: Hovering an inbox, notification or board row changes its fill. Taste observed no fill-changing hover and prefers a 1px outline at radius 6, or nothing.
findings.rule: 7.8 hover and selected
findings.fix: Documented decision: the components README allows 'hover fills only for fine pointers (`hover-fine:`)'. If kept, the selected fill must differ clearly from it (see the selected-row finding); accent-tint against surface-alt does.

findings.file: components/inbox/empty-states.tsx:323-494 (112px line art per reason), components/ui/empty.tsx:133-139
findings.issue: Queue-empty, not-connected, importing and import-failed states draw a 112px (`size-28`) line-art illustration over the sentence. Taste replaces illustrations with one sentence in the kept frame and the first action where the data will appear.
findings.rule: 11 empty/first run; 14 'an illustration and No data yet'
findings.fix: Documented decision: modelled on Notion Mail's inbox-zero art (empty-states.tsx:323-330), monochrome, with no illustration for filtered results. To follow Taste, drop `illustration` for queue_empty and checked (keep the sentence and action), and keep art only for first-run states.

findings.file: components/ui/tabs.tsx:210-211 (TabCount returns null for zero); components/inbox/queue-tabs.tsx:121-160
findings.issue: A queue or tab with 0 items shows no figure, while Taste prints a real zero ('0').
findings.rule: 11 a real zero is printed
findings.fix: Documented primitive behaviour (isZeroCount). Hiding is defensible in a tab strip, because 'Failed 0' adds noise. If adopted, print `0` in text-ink-muted for queues where zero is news (Failed, Approval) only.

summary: Visual pass of the running fixture app (http://localhost:3200, owner role, seeded journey tenant). I captured 9 routes at 390/768/1440 in light, plus /inbox and /design-system in dark at 1440: 29 PNGs in test-results/taste/before/. Every shoot.mjs JSON line reported status 200, horizontalOverflow:false and errors:[]. Nothing 404'd and /design-system rendered for owner. I followed each screenshot with a Playwright measurement pass (computed styles, rects, pseudo-element hit areas, with touch emulation at 390), so most findings below are measured, not guessed. Overall the shell is in good shape: one green accent, pale-tint pills with dark same-hue ink (6px radius, 22px tall, 12px), 12px/500 grey sentence-case table headers, no zebra striping, real zeros ('0%'), a phone tab bar of 56x76 targets, and chips and switches that look small (28px, 36x20) but have 44px hit areas. The clearest defects are: (1) the hours day card on desk, where rows sit 5px from the card border because the phone bleed (-mx-2) is never undone under desk; (2) Reports, which shows a 28px full-size em dash as a KPI value, a ~112px dead band between the tabs and the KPIs, and period facts that disagree (1 Oct – 29 Oct vs As at 30 Oct and an x-axis ending 30 Oct); (3) Listings, which drops Verification and Last published below 1100px and puts its primary action under the table while sibling Clients puts it in the title row; (4) a service-hours load failure on the hours page shown as plain text with no Retry, directly above 'No service schedules yet.'. The 12px card radius, the surface-alt table-head band and the green active-nav tint are documented decisions, so I report them as tensions. One environment caveat: the next-dev 'N' indicator (bottom-left) covers the sidebar profile avatar and the phone Inbox tab badge in every capture. It is dev chrome, not an app defect.

findings.issue: Inside the bordered 12px-radius 'Regular hours' card the day label starts at x=277 while the card edge is at x=272, and the switch ends at x=1403 against a card right edge of 1408. That leaves about 4px of inner padding plus the 1px border, so the toggles touch the rounded corners at 768 and 1440. The row uses rowBleedClassName '-mx-2 w-auto px-2' plus 'desk:px-2' but never resets the -8px margin under desk. The comment at :255-257 says 'the desk card puts them back inside its border', and the sibling row at :802 does that correctly with 'desk:mx-0'.
findings.rule: Spacing on a 4px base, card padding 12-34px (9.4); one left edge per block (4.2)
findings.fix: Add 'desk:mx-0' to the weekly row className (as at :802) and give the desk rows the card's inner padding (px-4/16px, the same inset as SettingsGroup content), so labels and switches sit 16px inside the border.

findings.issue: A missing median renders '—' at the KPI value size: computed font-size 28px in the ink colour (lab 9.5). In the 4-up row it reads as a loading placeholder next to '2', '0%' and '4.5'. The code comment at :33 documents the choice of a dash over 0, and the dash itself is right; what breaks the rule is its size and weight.
findings.rule: Missing or not applicable is a grey dash, never a dash at full value size (11)
findings.fix: In KpiTile, when value is the em dash, render it in text-ink-muted at the label size (text-ui, 13-14px) or as a 6x2px muted bar at the value's baseline, keeping the tile height. Optionally add 'No replies yet' as the subline instead of 'Review received to first reply'.

findings.issue: The tablist ends at y=293, the 'As at 30 Oct' caption sits at y=355 and the KPI tiles start at y=405. That is about 112px of near-empty band holding only a 12px grey stamp and a lone kebab at x=1390, larger than the 64px allowance before a section's content. The first figure is pushed below 400px on a 900px desktop screen.
findings.rule: panel-void: blank band over 40px inside a block (2.7, check 2); freshness stamp belongs beside the data (11)
findings.fix: Put the 'As at' stamp and the kebab on the same row as the Client/Period controls (right-aligned, after '2 listings · 1 Oct – 29 Oct'), or make them the KPI group's header row with a --np-space gap of 12-16px above the tiles.

findings.issue: One screen states the period three ways that disagree: the filter caption says '2 listings · 1 Oct – 29 Oct', the stamp says 'As at 30 Oct', and both charts say 'Latest day · 30 Oct' with x-axes ending '30 Oct'. A reader cannot tell whether 30 Oct is inside the 28-day window. Likely a UTC vs local day boundary in the fixture clock, but the screen shows it.
findings.rule: Every fact that appears twice must agree (2.7, check 4)
findings.fix: Derive the caption range, the 'As at' date and the chart domain from one period object in the same timezone (the organisation's). If 'As at' is a fetch timestamp rather than a period end, label it 'Updated 30 Oct, 09:14' so it doesn't read as a range end.

findings.component: Listings list below the desk table (tablet and phone)
findings.issue: At 1440 each row carries Listing, Client, Health, Waiting, Verification and Last published. At 768 and 390 the row keeps only name, client, 'Nothing waiting' and the health pill. Verification ('Verified' green pill) and Last published ('Never') are dropped, not moved to a subline. At 390 the identity also wraps ('Stub location / 48bf804e' on two lines) while the 107px pill holds the right column.
findings.rule: Tables become two-line rows; fields move to line 2, never dropped; tablet keeps 4-5 columns; the identity is never the column truncated (12)
findings.fix: Add a 13px text-ink-muted line-2 'Verified · Last published never' (verification as text, or the same 22px pill) to the card row. At 641-1100px keep the table with Verification and Last published folded under Health as a subline, and let the pill wrap under the name on phones instead of squeezing the name.

findings.component: Primary action placement, Listings vs Clients
findings.issue: On Listings the one filled-green primary 'Add listings from Google' (36px, radius 8) sits under the table at x=272, y=455, so its position moves with the row count. On the sibling list screen Clients, the primary 'New client' sits in the title row at the right edge (x≈1288-1408, y=107). Two list screens put their primary action in two different places.
findings.rule: The title row carries the screen's one primary action (4.3); one primary per surface
findings.fix: Move 'Add listings from Google' into the Listings title row, right-aligned like Clients' 'New client'. Keep a ghost or text 'Add listings' under the table only in the empty or first-run state.

findings.issue: The failure renders as plain 13px text-ink-secondary body copy ('Some service options couldn't load, so adding services is unavailable. Try again later.'). It has no role/status, no Retry, and no last-good time. Directly under it, 'No service schedules yet.' still renders, because the else-branch only checks !serviceNote for the category message. The block therefore claims a confirmed empty state for data it failed to read.
findings.rule: Error inside the block: one sentence of what failed and when, plus a Retry text button; honest empty states (11)
findings.fix: When serviceNote is the SERVICE_OPTIONS_WARNING, render it as the block's error line (small negative icon, role='status') with a 'Retry' ghost button that refetches the options. Suppress the 'No service schedules yet.' line in that state, or say 'Existing service schedules: none' only when moreHours was actually read.

findings.component: Hours page title row: Activity button
findings.issue: The h1 'Opening hours' (28px) starts at y=128 with its centre at about 146. The 36px 'Activity' outline button sits at y=156 with its centre at about 174, level with the subtitle 'Regular hours and special days' rather than the title, so it floats about 28px below the title's line. Separately, the breadcrumb at 1440 collapses the location name to '...' ('Listings / ... / Opening hours') with over 350px free before the status chip.
findings.rule: One left edge, one right edge; header actions align to the title row (4.2/4.3)
findings.fix: Align the header's action column to the h1 (items-start, or put Activity in the same flex row as the title and pill). Only collapse breadcrumb segments when the container query says they don't fit.

findings.component: Hours: same fact in two hues
findings.issue: 'No hours on Google' appears twice within 230px: as an amber warning pill beside the h1 (y≈146) and as a blue info callout (y 301-373) with its own blue icon. The same state carries warning amber in one place and info blue in the other.
findings.rule: Colour only on status, one status colour per fact; red/amber is a signal not a texture (9.2, 11)
findings.fix: Keep the title pill as the status and make the callout neutral (surface-alt, ink icon) as the explanation, or give the callout the warning tone so both copies share it. Never use info blue for a fact the pill calls a warning.

findings.issue: Measured: with post_scheduling off, the nav has no Calendar link on /inbox (navCalendar=false), but on /calendar the link appears (true) between Clients and Reports. That pushes Reports, Workspace, Team and Settings down 36px. The nav changes shape depending on the current page, and the page's own title is 'Publication calendar' while the nav says 'Calendar'.
findings.rule: Shell stability: the sidebar is a fixed map of destinations (3.2)
findings.fix: Either keep Calendar out of the nav whenever hideCalendar is true, even on /calendar (the page's own empty state explains why), or show it consistently. Match the h1 to the nav label ('Calendar').

findings.issue: At 1440 the h1 and content column start at x=332 on Settings, Notifications and Calendar, but at x=272 on Listings, Clients, Reports and Hours. Moving between nav items, the title jumps 60px horizontally. Notifications is a list, not a form, so the reading-width argument for a narrow centred column doesn't apply to it.
findings.rule: One left edge (4.2); width and gutters (4.1)
findings.fix: Start every page container at the same gutter (272 at 1440) and cap form width with max-w on the content inside, not by centring the whole column. At minimum, move Notifications and Calendar to the list-screen container.

findings.issue: Each empty state is a 44px grey rounded-square icon tile, a heading and a centred 12-13px paragraph, floated about 180-200px below the tabs or title in an empty canvas (Notifications block centre y≈490, Calendar y≈380). Notifications also repeats its action: a 'Notification settings' text button in the title row (ending x≈1333, which is 15px short of the 1348 edge used by '0 open and unread') and a 'Notification settings' outline button in the empty block. Calendar's explanation is a 4-line centred paragraph at about 12.5px.
findings.rule: Empty section keeps its frame and header with one sentence spanning the block; no icon-in-tinted-square; one right edge (11, 9.4, 4.2)
findings.fix: Render the empty list as the list's own frame: a 1px dashed --np line box, radius 8, about 40-56px tall, directly under the tabs, holding one 14px sentence. Drop the icon tile and the duplicate settings button, and align the title-row action to the content right edge. On Calendar, set the explanation left-aligned at text-ui (14px) under the title.

findings.issue: In the single-pane list at 768 the date ('28 Oct') ends at x≈730 on line 1, while the row kebab sits on line 2 ending at x≈754. The trailing column has two right edges 24px apart, and the kebab hangs below the date instead of aligning with it. At 1440 the kebab and date share an edge (667/690), so only this band is ragged.
findings.rule: One right edge (4.2); row actions as one compact trailing control (12)
findings.fix: Put the date and kebab in one trailing column with a shared right edge (kebab beside the date on line 1, or date right-aligned to the kebab's right edge).

findings.file: components/inbox (search dock), components/listings & clients filter inputs (screens: test-results/taste/before/inbox-chromium-light-390.png, listings-chromium-light-390.png)
findings.issue: With touch emulation at 390, 'Search reviews' measures 213x42 and 'Search listings or clients' / 'Filter clients by name' 309x42, with no expanded hit area. Every other control on these screens is 44px or carries a 44px pseudo-element hit band (chips 28+8+8, switches 20+12+12, kebabs 36+5+5). The mobile spec says fields are 44px on touch.
findings.rule: Phone: touch targets at least 44px (12); docs/specs/2026-10-13-mobile-first-design-system.md:97
findings.fix: Give the search field the field control height token on touch (--np-control-h, 44px) instead of the 42px value it is getting now.

findings.file: components/inbox/review-detail.tsx; listings/clients client avatar (screens: inbox-chromium-light-1440.png, listings-chromium-light-1440.png, clients-chromium-light-1440.png)
findings.issue: Three avatar treatments on neighbouring screens: reviewer 'SR' is a 32-44px grey circle, reply-as-location 'SL' a grey rounded square (≈44px, radius ≈8), and client 'JH' a solid slate rounded square with white initials (32px). The solid slate tile is the heaviest non-data ink in the Listings table.
findings.rule: Media in rows: one treatment per kind; colour on data not chrome (7.7, 9.2)
findings.fix: Use circles for people and one neutral rounded square (fill token, ink-secondary initials) for businesses and locations, and drop the solid slate fill so client identity doesn't outweigh the health pill.

findings.issue: Five Foundations cards in a 3-column grid leave an orphan empty cell (row 2, x≈897-1228, y≈521-664). The cards use a fill-only surface (surface-alt, no border) while the Neutrals swatch cards directly below use a 1px border on white, so the reference page shows two edge treatments for the same card role.
findings.rule: Orphan cell / ragged row (2.7, check 2); a border or a fill, one surface language (9.4)
findings.fix: Lay the five principles out as a divided list (one container, 1px line dividers) or as 3+2 with the second row spanning, and give them the same bordered card the swatches use.

findings.issue: Measured: KPI tiles, chart cards, the listings table frame, the settings group cards and the hours card are all border-radius 12px with a 1px line border and no shadow. Taste puts 11-12px in the weak middle (tight 4-8 or soft 16-24). Nested radii step only 12 -> 8 (controls) -> 6 (pills), and the settings warning callout inside a 12px card is about 10px, so there is almost no visible step.
findings.rule: Radius bimodal; nested radii step down (9.4)
findings.fix: Taste: move --np-radius-card to 8 (tight, matching 8px controls) or 16 (soft, with --np-radius-field/control at 8-10). System: radius 12 is the stated identity ('white cards drawn by a 1px line at radius 12'). If kept, at least make nested callouts 8 so the step reads.

findings.file: components/ui table primitive (th uses surface-alt) (screens: listings-chromium-light-1440.png, clients-chromium-light-1440.png)
findings.issue: Header cells are 12px, weight 500, grey (lab 42), left-aligned, 40px tall, which matches Taste. But the header row has a surface-alt fill (lab 96 on a white table), a filled band that 0 of 11 studied tables use. /design-system documents surface-alt as 'Sunken rows, rails, table head'.
findings.rule: Table header: no fill band (7.2)
findings.fix: Taste: drop the th background and keep the bottom hairline as the strongest rule. System: the surface-alt table head is a documented token role. If kept, make sure no other sunken element on the same screen uses surface-alt, so the band reads only as 'header'.

findings.component: Green active nav item and filter chips
findings.file: app-shell sidebar; docs/specs/2026-09-23-operators-desk-identity.md:39 ('One green accent. The primary action, focus, the current nav item') (screens: all *-1440.png)
findings.issue: The current sidebar item has a green tint fill (about 224px x 34px) plus a 3px green left bar and green ink. Active filter chips ('All 2', 'All 1', 'Last 28 days') also carry a green outline and tint. So the accent appears on chrome on every screen, while the selected inbox row uses a grey fill and a 3px near-black bar: two selection languages side by side on /inbox.
findings.rule: Colour on data, status and the one primary action, not chrome (9.2)
